sentences.zh: 李芳馮保張鯨陳增

translations.literal: Li Fang, Feng Bao, Zhang Jing, Chen Zeng
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, Feng Bao, Zhang Jing, and Chen Zeng

sentences.zh: 〈（陳奉高淮梁永楊榮）〉

translations.literal: (Chen Feng, Gao Huai, Liang Yong, Yang Rong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Chen Feng, Gao Huai, Liang Yong, and Yang Rong)〉

sentences.zh: 陳矩王安魏忠賢王體乾

translations.literal: Chen Ju, Wang An, Wei Zhongxian, Wang Tigan
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ju, Wang An, Wei Zhongxian, and Wang Tigan

sentences.zh: 〈（李永貞等）〉

translations.literal: (Li Yongzhen et al.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Li Yongzhen and others)〉

sentences.zh: 崔文升張彜憲高起潛王承恩方正化

translations.literal: Cui Wensheng, Zhang Yixian, Gao Qiqian, Wang Chengen, Fang Zhenghua
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng, Zhang Yixian, Gao Qiqian, Wang Chengen, and Fang Zhenghua

sentences.zh: 李芳，穆宗朝內官監太監也。

translations.literal: Li Fang was a eunuch of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs in the Muzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang served as a supervising eunuch of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs under Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 帝初立，芳以能持正見信任。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, Fang was trusted for his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first ascended the throne, Fang won trust because he could uphold what was right.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗時，匠役徐杲以營造躐官工部尚書，修盧溝橋，所侵盜萬計。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Shizong reign, the artisan Xu Gao had leapt by construction work to the post of Minister of Works, and in repairing the Lugou Bridge had embezzled on the order of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Jiajing reign, the craftsman Xu Gao had vaulted by palace construction to Minister of Works; while repairing the Lugou Bridge he had embezzled sums reckoned in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 其屬冒太僕少卿、苑馬卿以下職銜者以百數。

translations.literal: His subordinates had falsely taken titles down to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Director of the Imperial Parks, numbering in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: His followers had usurped ranks as low as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Director of the Imperial Parks—well over a hundred such cases.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年二月，芳劾之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Longqing, Fang impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Longqing 1, Fang impeached him.

sentences.zh: 時杲已削官，乃下獄遣戍，盡汰其所冒冗員。

translations.literal: Xu Gao had already been stripped of office; he was then imprisoned and sent into exile, and all the superfluous posts he had seized were purged.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xu Gao had already been stripped of rank; he was thrown into prison and banished, and every post his men had falsely held was abolished.

sentences.zh: 又奏革上林苑監增設皂隸，減光祿歲增米鹽及工部物料，以是大為同類所嫉。

translations.literal: Fang also memorialized to abolish the added runners at the Shanglin Park Directorate, and to cut the yearly increases in grain and salt for the Imperial Household and in materials for the Ministry of Works; for this he was greatly envied by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged abolishing extra runners at the Shanglin Park Directorate and trimming the annual increases in grain, salt, and Ministry of Works supplies—moves that made his fellow eunuchs hate him.

sentences.zh: 而是時，司禮諸閹滕祥、孟沖、陳洪方有寵，爭飾奇技淫巧以悅帝意，作鰲山燈，導帝為長夜飲。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial Teng Xiang, Meng Chong, and Chen Hong were in favor, each vying to display strange skills and wanton crafts to please the emperor, making Tortoise Mountain lamps and leading the emperor into all-night drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the favored eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial—Teng Xiang, Meng Chong, and Chen Hong—competed in bizarre luxuries to please the emperor, built Tortoise Mountain lamps, and drew him into nights of ceaseless drinking.

sentences.zh: 芳切諫，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Fang remonstrated sharply; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fang remonstrated bluntly, and the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 祥等復媒孽之，帝遂怒，勒芳閑住。

translations.literal: Xiang and the others again slandered him; the emperor grew angry and ordered Fang to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: They slandered him again; the emperor flew into a rage and forced Fang into idle retirement.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月復杖芳八十，下刑部監禁待決。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year he was again beaten with the rod eighty times and sent to the Ministry of Justice prison to await sentence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year two he was beaten eighty strokes with the rod and held in the Ministry of Justice prison awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書毛愷等言：「芳罪狀未明，臣等莫知所坐。」

translations.literal: Minister Mao Kai and others said: "Fang's offenses are not yet clear; your servants do not know what crime he has committed."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Mao Kai and others said, "Fang's guilt is still unclear—we do not know what charge he faces.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「芳事朕無禮，其錮之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Fang has been disrespectful to Us; confine him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Fang has treated Us without proper respect—put him in confinement."

sentences.zh: 芳錮，祥等益橫。

translations.literal: Once Fang was confined, Xiang and the others grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: With Fang confined, Xiang and his allies grew bolder than ever.

sentences.zh: 前司禮太監黃錦已革蔭，祥輒復予之。

translations.literal: The former Director of Ceremonial Huang Jin had already had his hereditary privilege revoked, yet Xiang promptly restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jin, the former Director of Ceremonial, had already lost his hereditary privilege, but Xiang immediately restored it.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書雷禮劾祥：「傳造采辦器物及修補壇廟樂器，多自加徵，糜費巨萬。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lei Li impeached Xiang: "In commissioning and procuring objects and in repairing altar and temple instruments, he often added his own surcharges, wasting tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lei Li impeached Xiang: "In palace commissions and repairs to ritual instruments he piled on extra levies and squandered vast sums.

sentences.zh: 工廠存留大木，斬截任意。

translations.literal: Timber kept at the workshops was cut up at will.
translations.idiomatic: Stockpiled timber at the workshops was hacked apart as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 臣禮力不能爭，乞早賜罷。」

translations.literal: Your servant Li lacks the strength to contend; I beg to be dismissed early."
translations.idiomatic: I lack the power to fight him; please dismiss me at once.

sentences.zh: 帝不罪祥，而令禮致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish Xiang but ordered Li to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish Xiang; he let Li retire instead.

sentences.zh: 沖傳旨下海戶王印於鎮撫司，論戍，法司不預聞。

translations.literal: Chong transmitted an edict sending the maritime household Wang Yin to the Brocade Guard prison for exile; the judicial offices were not consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chong sent down an edict consigning the maritime household Wang Yin to the Brocade Guard for banishment without the law courts hearing the case.

sentences.zh: 納肅藩輔國將軍縉貴賄，越制得嗣封肅王。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes from the Su princedom's auxiliary-state general Jin Gui and, contrary to regulation, secured the succession as Prince of Su.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes from Jin Gui, auxiliary-state general of the Su princedom, and bent the rules so Jin could inherit as Prince of Su.

sentences.zh: 洪尤貪肆，內閣大臣亦有因之以進者。

translations.literal: Hong was especially greedy and unrestrained; even grand secretaries advanced through him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hong was greedier still, and even chief grand secretaries owed their rise to him.

sentences.zh: 三人所糜國帑無算。

translations.literal: The three of them squandered the state treasury beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Between them they drained the treasury beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 帝享太廟，三人皆冠進賢冠，服祭服以從，爵賞辭謝與六卿埒。

translations.literal: When the emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, all three wore the Advancement of Worthies cap and sacrificial robes in attendance; in titles, rewards, and polite refusals they ranked with the six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial ancestral sacrifice all three wore the Advancement of Worthies cap and ritual dress beside the emperor, matching the six ministers in rank, honors, and ceremonial precedence.

sentences.zh: 廷臣論劾者，太常少卿周審怡以外補去，給事中石星、李已、陳吾德，御史詹仰庇，尚寶丞鄭履淳，皆廷杖削籍。

translations.literal: Court officials who impeached them: Vice Minister of Rites Zhou Shenyi was transferred outside the capital; supervising secretaries Shi Xing, Li Yi, and Chen Wude, censor Zhan Yangbi, and Court of Imperial Entertainments director Zheng Luchun were all beaten at court and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Critics paid dearly: Zhou Shenyi was posted away; Shi Xing, Li Yi, Chen Wude, Zhan Yangbi, and Zheng Luchun were flogged at court and expelled from office.

sentences.zh: 三人各蔭錦衣官至二十人，而芳獨久系獄。

translations.literal: Each of the three secured hereditary posts in the Brocade Guard for as many as twenty men, while Fang alone languished long in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Each secured Brocade Guard sinecures for up to twenty kinsmen, while Fang alone rotted in jail.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，刑科都給事中舒化等以熱審屆期，請宥芳，乃得釋，充南京凈軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Chief Supervising Secretary Shu Hua and others, as the summer review of prisoners drew near, asked that Fang be pardoned; he was released and made a purifying soldier in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year four, as the summer prison review approached, Shu Hua and others secured Fang's release; he was sent to Nanjing as a purifying soldier.

sentences.zh: 穆宗甫崩，保言於后妃，斥孟沖而奪其位，又矯遺詔令與閣臣同受顧命。

translations.literal: As soon as Muzong died, Bao spoke to the empresses and consorts, drove out Meng Chong and seized his post, and also forged the testamentary edict so that he and the grand secretaries alike received the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Muzong died, Bao persuaded the palace women to oust Meng Chong and seize his office, and forged the testamentary edict naming himself among the regents with the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 及帝登極，保升立寶座旁不下，舉朝大駭。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Bao stood beside the throne and did not step down; the whole court was appalled.
translations.idiomatic: At the accession Bao mounted the dais beside the throne and refused to descend—the court was horrified.

sentences.zh: 保既掌司禮，又督東廠，兼總內外，勢益張。

translations.literal: Bao now held the Directorate of Ceremonial and supervised the Eastern Depot, controlling inner and outer affairs; his power grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Directorate of Ceremonial, ran the Eastern Depot, and dominated court and camp alike.

sentences.zh: 拱諷六科給事中程文、十三道御史劉良弼等，交章數其奸，而給事中雒遵、陸樹德又特疏論列，拱意疏下即擬旨逐保。

translations.literal: Gong induced the supervising secretaries of the six bureaus Cheng Wen and the thirteen circuit censors Liu Liangbi and others to submit joint memorials listing his crimes; supervising secretaries Luo Zun and Lu Shude also submitted special memorials; Gong intended that once the memorials arrived he would draft an edict expelling Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong prompted Cheng Wen, Liu Liangbi, and others to denounce Bao in waves of memorials; Luo Zun and Lu Shude added their own; Gong meant to draft an edict the moment the papers arrived.

sentences.zh: 而保匿其疏，亟與居正定謀，遂逐拱去。

translations.literal: But Bao hid the memorials, quickly plotted with Zhang Juzheng, and drove Gong away.
translations.idiomatic: Bao suppressed the papers, plotted with Zhang Juzheng, and ousted Gong instead.

sentences.zh: 初，穆宗崩，拱於閣中大慟曰：「十歲太子，如何治天下。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Muzong died, Gong had wailed in the Grand Secretariat: "A ten-year-old crown prince—how can he govern the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong died, Gong had wailed in the Grand Secretariat, "A ten-year-old heir—how will he rule the realm?

sentences.zh: 保譖於后妃曰：「拱斥太子為十歲孩子，如何作人主。」

translations.literal: Bao slandered him to the empresses and consorts, saying: "Gong calls the crown prince a ten-year-old child—how can he be sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao told the palace women Gong had mocked the heir as "a ten-year-old child unfit to be sovereign."

sentences.zh: 后妃大驚，太子聞之亦色變。

translations.literal: The empresses and consorts were greatly alarmed; when the crown prince heard it his face changed color.
translations.idiomatic: They were terrified; the crown prince turned pale when he heard.

sentences.zh: 迨拱去，保憾猶未釋。

translations.literal: After Gong left, Bao's resentment was still not spent.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Gong was gone, Bao's grudge had not cooled.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年正月，有王大臣者，偽為內侍服，入乾清宮，被獲下東廠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Wanli, one Wang Dachen, disguised as an inner attendant, entered the Palace of Heavenly Purity and was seized and sent to the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wanli 1, Wang Dachen entered the Palace of Heavenly Purity in palace dress and was seized by the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 保欲緣此族拱，與居正謀，令家人辛儒飲食之，納刃其袖中，俾言拱怨望，遣刺帝。

translations.literal: Bao wished to use this to destroy Gong's clan; he plotted with Juzheng, had his household retainer Xin Ru feed and clothe him, slip a blade into his sleeve, and make him say Gong bore resentment and had sent him to assassinate the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao meant to implicate Gong's whole clan; with Juzheng he fed Wang Dachen, hid a blade in his sleeve, and coached him to claim Gong had sent him to kill the emperor.

sentences.zh: 大臣許之。

translations.literal: Dachen agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dachen agreed.

sentences.zh: 逾日，錦衣都督朱希孝等會鞫。

translations.literal: The next day the Brocade Guard commander Zhu Xixiao and others jointly interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhu Xixiao of the Brocade Guard and others interrogated him jointly.

sentences.zh: 大臣疾呼曰：「許我富貴，乃掠治我耶！

translations.literal: Dachen cried out: "You promised me wealth and honor—now you torture me!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dachen shouted, "You promised me riches—now you torture me!

sentences.zh: 且我何處識高閣老？」

translations.literal: Besides, how would I know Senior Grand Secretary Gao?"
translations.idiomatic: And how would I even know Senior Grand Secretary Gao?

sentences.zh: 希孝懼，不敢鞫而罷。

translations.literal: Xixiao was afraid and dared not continue the interrogation and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xixiao, afraid, broke off the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 會廷臣楊博、葛守禮等保待之，居正亦迫眾議微諷保。

translations.literal: Court ministers Yang Bo, Ge Shouli, and others came to Bao's defense; Juzheng also, pressed by public opinion, subtly urged Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo, Ge Shouli, and others defended Bao; Juzheng, under public pressure, quietly warned him.

sentences.zh: 保意稍解，乃以生漆酒喑大臣，移送法司坐斬，拱獲免。

translations.literal: Bao's mind eased somewhat; he then used raw-lacquer wine to silence Dachen, transferred him to the law courts for execution, and Gong escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bao relented, silenced Wang with lacquer wine, sent him to the law courts for execution, and Gong was spared.

sentences.zh: 由是舉朝皆惡保，而不肖者多因之以進。

translations.literal: From this the whole court hated Bao, yet many unworthy men advanced through him.
translations.idiomatic: The court despised Bao, yet the unscrupulous still climbed by his favor.

sentences.zh: 慈聖太后遇帝嚴。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cisheng was strict with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cisheng kept the emperor on a short leash.

sentences.zh: 保倚太后勢，數挾持帝，帝甚畏之。

translations.literal: Bao relied on the empress dowager's power and repeatedly coerced the emperor, who greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao leaned on her authority and often bullied the emperor, who was deeply afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 時與小內豎戲，見保入，輒正襟危坐曰：「大伴來矣。」

translations.literal: When he played with the young eunuchs and saw Bao enter, he would straighten his robes and sit properly, saying: "Elder Companion is here."
translations.idiomatic: Playing with junior eunuchs, he would sit bolt upright at Bao's entrance and say, "Elder Companion is here.

sentences.zh: 所昵孫海、客用為乾清宮管事牌子，屢誘帝夜遊別宮，小衣窄袖，走馬持刀，又數進奇巧之物，帝深寵幸。

translations.literal: His favorites Sun Hai and Ke Yong, stewards of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, often lured the emperor to roam other palaces at night in tight sleeves and short coats, galloping with blades; they also repeatedly presented curious objects, and the emperor doted on them deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His favorites Sun Hai and Ke Yong, stewards of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, lured him on night rides in tight dress with sword in hand and fed him novelties—the emperor adored them.

sentences.zh: 保白太后，召帝切責。

translations.literal: Bao informed the empress dowager, who summoned the emperor and rebuked him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Bao told the empress dowager, who summoned the emperor and scolded him harshly.

sentences.zh: 帝長跪受教，惶懼甚。

translations.literal: The emperor knelt long to receive the lesson, utterly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knelt in terror through the lecture.

sentences.zh: 保屬居正草帝罪己手詔，令頒示閣臣。

translations.literal: Bao had Juzheng draft an imperial hand-edict of self-reproach for the emperor and ordered it shown to the grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had Juzheng draft a handwritten imperial confession and circulate it to the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 詞過挹損，帝年已十八，覽之內慚，然迫於太后，不得不下。

translations.literal: The wording was excessively self-abasing; the emperor was already eighteen, and reading it he felt inward shame, yet constrained by the empress dowager he had no choice but to issue it.
translations.idiomatic: The language was humiliating beyond measure; at eighteen the emperor burned with shame yet could not refuse the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 居正乃上疏切諫。

translations.literal: Juzheng then submitted a memorial of sharp remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng then memorialized in blunt protest.

sentences.zh: 又緣保意劾去司禮秉筆孫德秀、溫太及掌兵伏局周海，而令諸內侍俱自陳。

translations.literal: He also, at Bao's wish, impeached and removed the Ceremonial director Sun Dexiu, Wen Tai, and Zhou Hai who controlled the military depot, and ordered all inner attendants to report on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Bao's urging he purged Sun Dexiu, Wen Tai, and depot chief Zhou Hai and made every eunuch confess.

sentences.zh: 由是保所不悅者，斥退殆盡，時八年十一月也。

translations.literal: Thus those Bao disliked were nearly all expelled; this was in the eleventh month of the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month of year eight, Bao's enemies were nearly all gone.

sentences.zh: 保善琴能書。

translations.literal: Bao was skilled at the zither and could write.
translations.idiomatic: Bao played the zither well and wrote a fine hand.

sentences.zh: 帝屢賜牙章曰「光明正大」，曰「爾惟鹽梅」，曰「汝作舟楫」，曰「魚水相逢」，曰「風雲際會」，所以待之甚隆。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly bestowed ivory seals reading "Bright and Upright," "You Are the Salt and Plum," "You Are the Boat and Oar," "Fish and Water Meet," and "Wind and Cloud Join"; thus he was treated with the greatest honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him ivory seals inscribed "Bright and Upright," "You Are the Salt and Plum," "You Are the Boat and Oar," "Fish and Water Meet," and "Wind and Cloud Join"—honors rarely seen.

sentences.zh: 後保益橫肆，即帝有所賞罰，非出保口，無敢行者。

translations.literal: Later Bao grew still more overbearing; even when the emperor wished to reward or punish, unless it came from Bao's mouth no one dared act.
translations.idiomatic: Later even rewards and punishments required Bao's word before anyone dared carry them out.

sentences.zh: 帝積不能堪，而保內倚太后，外倚居正，帝不能去也。

translations.literal: The emperor could bear it no longer, yet Bao leaned on the empress dowager within and Juzheng without; the emperor could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seethed, but with the empress dowager within and Juzheng without, he could not oust Bao.

sentences.zh: 然保亦時引大體。

translations.literal: Yet Bao also sometimes upheld larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Bao sometimes upheld the larger good.

sentences.zh: 內閣產白蓮，翰林院有雙白燕，居正以進。

translations.literal: White lotus grew in the Grand Secretariat; twin white swallows appeared at the Hanlin Academy; Juzheng presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng presented a white lotus from the Grand Secretariat and twin white swallows from the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 保使使謂居正曰：「主上沖年，不可以異物啟玩好。」

translations.literal: Bao sent a messenger to tell Juzheng: "The sovereign is in his minority; strange things must not be used to stir his fondness for curios."
translations.idiomatic: Bao warned Juzheng, "The sovereign is young—do not feed his taste for wonders with such omens.

sentences.zh: 又能約束其子弟，不敢肆惡，都人亦以是稱之。

translations.literal: He could also restrain his sons and younger brothers from wanton evil; the capital people praised him for this as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept his kin from running wild, which won praise in the capital.

sentences.zh: 居正固有才，其所以得委任專國柄者，由保為之左右也。

translations.literal: Juzheng was talented by nature; that he received appointment and monopolized state power was because Bao supported him on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had real talent, but his monopoly on power owed everything to Bao's backing.

sentences.zh: 然保性貪，其私人錦衣指揮徐爵、內官張大受，為保、居正交關語言。

translations.literal: Yet Bao was greedy by nature; his private men, Brocade Guard commander Xu Jue and inner attendant Zhang Dashou, carried messages between Bao and Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bao was greedy; his creatures Xu Jue of the Brocade Guard and Zhang Dashou shuttled between him and Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 且數用計使兩人相疑，旋復相好，兩人皆在爵術中。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly used schemes to make the two suspect each other and then reconcile; both were caught in Jue's tricks.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly set them against each other and reconciled them again—both danced in Xu Jue's net.

sentences.zh: 事與籌畫，因恃勢招權利，大臣亦多與通。

translations.literal: They took part in planning; relying on power they sought profit, and many ministers also dealt with them.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted with him, traded on his power, and many ministers dealt through them.

sentences.zh: 爵夜至禁門，守衛者不敢詰，其橫如此。

translations.literal: Jue came to the forbidden gate at night and the guards dared not question him; such was his arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jue reached the palace gates at night unchallenged—such was their arrogance.

sentences.zh: 居正之奪情及杖吳中行等，保有力焉。

translations.literal: In Juzheng's refusal to leave mourning and in the beating of Wu Zhongxing and others, Bao had force.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had a hand in Juzheng's refusal to mourn and in flogging Wu Zhongxing and others.

sentences.zh: 已而居正死，其黨益結保自固。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, his faction clung all the more to Bao to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng died, his faction clung tighter to Bao.

sentences.zh: 居正以遺疏薦其座主潘晟入閣，保即遣官召之。

translations.literal: Juzheng in his death memorial had recommended his patron Pan Sheng for the Grand Secretariat; Bao at once sent officials to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's death memorial recommended his patron Pan Sheng for the Grand Secretariat; Bao immediately sent to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 御史雷士楨、王國，給事中王繼光相繼言其不可用，晟中途疏辭。

translations.literal: Censors Lei Shizhen and Wang Guo and supervising secretary Wang Jiguang in succession said he was unfit; Sheng memorialized to decline on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Lei Shizhen and Wang Guo and supervising secretary Wang Jiguang said Pan Sheng was unfit; Sheng declined en route.

sentences.zh: 內閣張四維度申時行不肯為晟下，擬旨允之，帝即報可。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Siwei guessed Shen Shixing would not draft the appointment for Sheng; they drafted an edict granting it, and the emperor at once approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siwei guessed Shen Shixing would not draft Sheng's appointment; they drafted approval and the emperor assented at once.

sentences.zh: 保時病起，詬曰：「我小恙，遽無我耶？」

translations.literal: Bao, then risen from illness, cursed: "I have a small ailment—are you done with me already?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao, just risen from illness, raged, "A little sickness and you write me off already?

sentences.zh: 皇太子生，保欲封伯爵，四維以無故事難之，擬蔭弟侄一人都督僉事。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was born, Bao wished to ennoble him as earl; Siwei objected that there was no precedent and drafted hereditary posts as regional commander for one younger brother and nephew.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was born, Bao wanted an earldom; Siwei cited precedent and offered only a regional command for a nephew.

sentences.zh: 保怒曰：「爾由誰得今日，而負我！」

translations.literal: Bao angrily said: "By whom did you get where you are today, yet you betray me!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao snarled, "Who made you what you are today—and this is how you repay me!

sentences.zh: 御史郭惟賢請召用吳中行等，保責其黨護，謫之。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Weixian asked to recall Wu Zhongxing and others; Bao accused him of factional protection and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Weixian asked to recall Wu Zhongxing and others; Bao called it factional favoritism and banished him.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王國光罷，保輒用其鄉人梁夢龍代。

translations.literal: When Minister of Personnel Wang Guoguang was dismissed, Bao at once replaced him with his townsman Liang Menglong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Guoguang left the Ministry of Personnel, Bao installed his townsman Liang Menglong.

sentences.zh: 爵、大受等竊權如故。

translations.literal: Jue, Dashou, and the others usurped power as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jue, Zhang Dashou, and the rest stole power as before.

sentences.zh: 然是時太后久歸政，保失所倚，帝又積怒保。

translations.literal: Yet by then the empress dowager had long returned power; Bao had lost his support, and the emperor had long nursed anger against Bao.
translations.idiomatic: By then the empress dowager had returned power; Bao had lost his pillar, and the emperor's wrath had piled up.

sentences.zh: 東宮舊閹張鯨、張誠乘間陳其過惡，請令閑住。

translations.literal: Former Eastern Palace eunuchs Zhang Jing and Zhang Cheng seized the moment to list his crimes and ask that he be made to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Old palace eunuchs Zhang Jing and Zhang Cheng seized the moment to list his crimes and ask that he retire.

sentences.zh: 帝猶畏之，曰：「若大伴上殿來，朕奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor still feared him and said: "If Elder Companion comes up to the hall, what can We do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still feared him: "If Elder Companion enters the hall, what can We do?

sentences.zh: 鯨曰：「既有旨，安敢復入。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Once there is an edict, how would he dare enter again."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "With an edict in force, he would not dare return."

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會御史李植、江東之彈章入，遂謫保奉御，南京安置，久之乃死。

translations.literal: When the impeachment memorials of censors Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi arrived, Bao was demoted to palace attendant, settled in Nanjing, and after a long time died.
translations.idiomatic: When censors Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi impeached him, Bao was demoted to palace attendant in Nanjing, where he died after long years.

sentences.zh: 其弟佑、從子邦寧並官都督，削職下獄，瘐死。

translations.literal: His younger brother You and nephew Bangning, both regional commanders, were stripped of office and imprisoned and died of illness in jail.
translations.idiomatic: His brother You and nephew Bangning, both regional commanders, were stripped, jailed, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 大受及其黨周海、何忠等八人，貶小火者，司香孝陵。

translations.literal: Dashou and his faction Zhou Hai, He Zhong, and eight others were demoted to junior fire-tenders tending incense at the Xiaoling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dashou and eight allies including Zhou Hai and He Zhong were demoted to tend incense at the Xiaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 爵與大受子，煙瘴永戍。

translations.literal: Jue and Dashou's sons were forever exiled to miasmic border regions.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jue and Zhang Dashou's sons were exiled for life to the southern miasma.

sentences.zh: 盡籍其家，保金銀百餘萬，珠寶瑰異稱是。

translations.literal: Their households were fully confiscated; Bao's gold and silver exceeded a million, and jewels and rarities matched that sum.
translations.idiomatic: Their property was seized; Bao alone held over a million in gold and silver, with gems to match.

sentences.zh: 保之發南京也，太后問故。

translations.literal: When Bao was sent off from Nanjing, the empress dowager asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao left for Nanjing, the empress dowager asked why.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「老奴為張居正所惑，無他過，行且召還。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The old slave was misled by Zhang Juzheng; he has no other fault and will soon be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The old servant was led astray by Zhang Juzheng—no other fault; We shall recall him soon.

sentences.zh: 時潞王將婚，所需珠寶未備，太后間以為言。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Lu was about to marry and the jewels needed were not yet ready; the empress dowager occasionally mentioned it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu's wedding jewels were still lacking, and the empress dowager brought it up from time to time.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「年來無恥臣僚，盡貨以獻張、馮二家，其價驟貴。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In recent years shameless officials have sold everything to present to the Zhang and Feng households, and prices have soared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shameless officials have been selling everything to the Zhang and Feng cliques, and prices have shot up.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「已籍矣，必可得。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "They have been confiscated—surely they can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "His property was seized—you can surely get them."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奴黠猾，先竊而逃，未能盡得也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The slave is cunning and slipped away with much of it first; We could not get it all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The old rogue was sly—he stole away with the best before we could take it all."

sentences.zh: 而其時，錦衣都督劉守有與僚屬張昭、龐清、馮昕等，皆以籍罪人家，多所隱沒，得罪。

translations.literal: At that time the Brocade Guard commander Liu Shouyou and his subordinates Zhang Zhao, Pang Qing, Feng Xin, and others, all having seized the property of convicted households, concealed much of it and were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Shouyou of the Brocade Guard and his men Zhang Zhao, Pang Qing, and Feng Xin, who had looted convicted estates and hidden the takings, were punished.

sentences.zh: 張鯨，新城人，太監張宏名下也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing was a man of Xincheng and served under the eunuch Zhang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing of Xincheng had entered service under the eunuch Zhang Hong.

sentences.zh: 內豎初入宮，必投一大珰為主，謂之名下。

translations.literal: When a young eunuch first entered the palace he had to attach himself to a senior eunuch as patron—this was called "under a name."
translations.idiomatic: Junior eunuchs had to attach to a senior patron—called being "under his name."

sentences.zh: 馮保用事，鯨害其寵，為帝畫策害保。

translations.literal: When Feng Bao held power, Jing resented his favor and plotted with the emperor to destroy Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resented Feng Bao's favor and coached the emperor in schemes against him.

sentences.zh: 寵謂鯨曰：「馮公前輩，且有骨力，不宜去之。」

translations.literal: Hong said to Jing: "Director Feng is a senior with backbone; he should not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong warned Jing, "Director Feng is a senior with backbone—you should not remove him.

sentences.zh: 鯨不聽。

translations.literal: Jing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既譖逐保，宏遂代保掌司禮監，而鯨掌東廠。

translations.literal: After slandering and driving out Bao, Hong took Bao's place as Director of Ceremonial, and Jing controlled the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bao was ousted, Hong became Director of Ceremonial and Jing ran the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 宏無過惡，以賢稱，萬曆十二年卒。

translations.literal: Hong had no great faults and was praised as worthy; he died in the twelfth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was regarded as virtuous and died in Wanli 12.

sentences.zh: 張誠代掌司禮監。

translations.literal: Zhang Cheng replaced him as Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng succeeded him at the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 十八年，鯨罷東廠，誠兼掌之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Jing was removed from the Eastern Depot and Cheng took charge of it as well.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen Jing left the Eastern Depot and Cheng took it over.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，以誠聯姻武清侯，擅作威福，降奉御，司香孝陵，籍其家，弟侄皆削職治罪。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, because Cheng had married into the Wuqing marquis's family and abused his power, he was demoted to palace attendant tending incense at the Xiaoling tomb; his property was confiscated and his younger brothers and nephews were stripped of office and punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty-four Cheng was demoted for marrying into the Wuqing marquisate and lording it over others; his estate was seized and his kin punished.

sentences.zh: 鯨性剛果，帝倚任之。

translations.literal: Jing was firm and resolute by nature, and the emperor relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was bold and decisive, and the emperor leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 其在東廠兼掌內府供用庫印，頗為時相所憚。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Depot he also held the seal of the inner palace supply depot and was much feared by chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Eastern Depot and the inner supply depot seal, and chief ministers feared him.

sentences.zh: 而其用事司房邢尚智，招權受賕。

translations.literal: His agent Xing Shangzhi abused power and took bribes.
translations.idiomatic: His clerk Xing Shangzhi traded on his power for bribes.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年冬，御史何出光劾鯨及其黨鴻臚序班尚智與錦衣都督劉守有相倚為奸，專擅威福，罪當死者八。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year of Wanli, censor He Chuguang impeached Jing and his clique, the protocol officer Shangzhi and Brocade Guard commander Liu Shouyou, for relying on each other in wickedness and monopolizing power—eight crimes warranting death.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 16, censor He Chuguang impeached Jing, Shangzhi, and Liu Shouyou for eight capital crimes of shared tyranny.

sentences.zh: 帝命鯨策勵供事，而削尚智、守有職，余黨法司提問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jing to redouble his service while stripping Shangzhi and Shouyou of office; the rest were handed to the law courts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Jing to serve harder, stripped Shangzhi and Shouyou, and sent the rest to the law courts.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳尚象、吳文梓、楊文煥，御史方萬策、崔景榮復相繼論列，報聞。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Chen Shangxiang, Wu Wenzhi, and Yang Wenhuan and censors Fang Wance and Cui Jingrong memorialized in succession; the response was acknowledgment only.
translations.idiomatic: More memorials followed from Chen Shangxiang, Wu Wenzhi, Yang Wenhuan, Fang Wance, and Cui Jingrong—to no effect.

sentences.zh: 法司奏鯨等贓罪，尚智論死，鯨被切責。

translations.literal: The law courts reported Jing's and others' corruption; Shangzhi was sentenced to death and Jing was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The law courts convicted them; Shangzhi was sentenced to death and Jing was scolded.

sentences.zh: 給事中張應登再疏論之，御史馬象乾並劾大學士申時行阿縱。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhang Yingdeng memorialized again, and censor Ma Xiangqian also impeached Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing for indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingdeng memorialized again; censor Ma Xiangqian impeached Shen Shixing for indulging Jing.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽，命下象乾詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen and sent Xiangqian to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and sent Ma Xiangqian to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 以時行及同官許國、王錫爵等申救，象乾疏乃留中。

translations.literal: Because Shixing and his colleagues Xu Guo and Wang Xijue pleaded for mercy, Xiangqian's memorial was held in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing, Xu Guo, and Wang Xijue interceded, and Ma Xiangqian's memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 給事中李沂至謂帝納鯨金寶，故寬鯨罪。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Li Yi even said the emperor had accepted Jing's gold and jewels and therefore leniently treated Jing's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi went so far as to say the emperor had taken Jing's gold and gems and therefore spared him.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，言沂等為張居正、馮保報復，杖六十，削其官，鯨亦私家閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, saying Yi and the others were avenging Zhang Juzheng and Feng Bao; he beat them sixty strokes and struck them from office; Jing was also made to live in private retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged that they avenged Juzheng and Bao, flogged Li Yi sixty strokes and expelled him, and put Jing in private retirement.

sentences.zh: 已而南京兵部尚書吳文華率南九卿請罪鯨而宥言者，帝亦不聽。

translations.literal: Later Nanjing Minister of War Wu Wenhua and the southern nine ministers asked to punish Jing and pardon the speakers; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Wenhua and the southern nine ministers asked to punish Jing and pardon the critics; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋復召鯨入。

translations.literal: Soon Jing was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing was recalled.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳與郊、御史賈希夷、南京吏部尚書陸光祖、給事中徐常吉、御史王以通等言益力，俱不報。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Chen Yuhe and Jia Xiyi, Nanjing Minister of Personnel Lu Guangzu, supervising secretaries Xu Changji and censor Wang Yitong and others spoke still more forcefully; all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuhe, Jia Xiyi, Lu Guangzu, Xu Changji, Wang Yitong, and others pressed harder—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 最後大理評事雒於仁上酒色財氣四箴，指鯨以賄復進。

translations.literal: Finally Court of Review clerk Luo Yuren submitted the four admonitions on wine, sex, wealth, and wrath, pointing to Jing's restoration through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Luo Yuren of the Court of Review submitted his four admonitions on wine, sex, wealth, and wrath, naming Jing's bribe-fueled return.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，召申時行等於毓德宮，命治於仁罪，而召鯨，令時行等傳諭責訓之，鯨寵遂衰。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry, summoned Shen Shixing and others to the Yude Palace, ordered Yuren punished, and summoned Jing, having Shixing and others transmit rebuke and instruction; Jing's favor then declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Shixing to Yude Palace to punish Luo Yuren, then summoned Jing for a dressing-down—and Jing's star fell.

sentences.zh: 尚智後減死充軍。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's sentence was later reduced to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's death sentence was later commuted to military exile.

sentences.zh: 陳奉 高淮 梁永 楊榮等

translations.literal: Chen Feng, Gao Huai, Liang Yong, Yang Rong, and others
translations.idiomatic: Chen Feng, Gao Huai, Liang Yong, Yang Rong, and others

sentences.zh: 陳增，神宗朝礦稅太監也。

translations.literal: Chen Zeng was a mining-tax eunuch of the Shenzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zeng was a mining-tax eunuch under Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十二年，房山縣民史錦奏請開礦，下撫按查勘，不果行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Wanli, Shi Jin of Fangshan county memorialized to open mines; the matter was sent to the grand coordinator and regional inspector for investigation and did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 12, Shi Jin of Fangshan asked to open mines; investigators blocked it.

sentences.zh: 十六年，中使祠五臺山，還言紫荊關外廣昌、靈丘有礦砂，可作銀冶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, palace envoys returning from worship at Wutai said that outside Zijing Pass at Guangchang and Lingqiu there was ore sand fit for silver smelting.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen, envoys from Wutai reported ore sand outside Zijing Pass at Guangchang and Lingqiu fit for silver.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之喜，以大學士申時行等言而止。

translations.literal: The emperor heard it with joy but stopped on the advice of Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted but Shen Shixing and others stopped him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，易州民周言、張世才復言阜平、房山各產礦砂，請遣官開礦。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Zhou Yan and Zhang Shicai of Yizhou again said Fuping and Fangshan each produced ore sand and asked that officials be sent to open mines.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen, Zhou Yan and Zhang Shicai of Yizhou again urged mining at Fuping and Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 時行等仍執不可。

translations.literal: Shixing and others still held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and others still refused.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，寧夏用兵，費帑金二百餘萬。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year, the Ningxia campaign had cost the treasury more than two million.
translations.idiomatic: By year twenty the Ningxia war had cost over two million taels.

sentences.zh: 其冬。

translations.literal: That winter.
translations.idiomatic: That winter,

sentences.zh: 朝鮮用兵，首尾八年，費帑金七百餘萬。

translations.literal: the Korean war, eight years from start to finish, cost the treasury more than seven million.
translations.idiomatic: the Korean war ran eight years and cost over seven million.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，播州用兵，又費帑金二三百萬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Bozhou campaign again cost two or three million.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven the Bozhou campaign cost another two or three million.

sentences.zh: 三大征踵接，國用大匱。

translations.literal: The three great campaigns followed one after another and state funds were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Three great campaigns in succession emptied the treasury.

sentences.zh: 而二十四年，乾清、坤寧兩宮災。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Palaces of Heavenly Purity and Earthly Tranquility burned.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four the Palaces of Heavenly Purity and Earthly Tranquility burned.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皇極、建極、中極三殿災。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the three halls of Supreme Pole, Middle Pole, and Establishing Pole burned.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five the three main halls burned.

sentences.zh: 營建乏資，計臣束手，礦稅由此大興矣。

translations.literal: Construction lacked funds and the finance ministers were helpless; mining taxes arose on this scale.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuild funds ran out and finance ministers were helpless—mining taxes exploded.

sentences.zh: 其遣官自二十四年始，其後言礦者爭走闕下，帝即命中官與其人偕往，天下在在有之。

translations.literal: Officials were first dispatched in the twenty-fourth year; afterward those who spoke of mines rushed to the capital gate and the emperor at once ordered eunuchs to go with them—everywhere under heaven had them.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch began in year twenty-four; then every petitioner at the gate won a eunuch partner—mines spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 真、保、薊、永則王亮，昌黎、遷安則田進，昌平、橫嶺、淶水、珠寶窩山則王忠，真定復益以王虎，並采山西平定、稷山，浙江則曹金，後代以劉忠，陜西則趙欽，山西則張忠，河南則魯坤，廣東則李鳳、李敬，雲南則楊榮，遼東則高淮，江西則潘相，福建則高寀，湖廣則陳奉，而增奉敕開采山東。

translations.literal: Zhending, Baoding, Ji, and Yong had Wang Liang; Changli and Qian'an had Tian Jin; Changping, Hengling, Laishui, and Jewel Mountain had Wang Zhong; Zhending added Wang Hu, also mining in Pingding and Jishan, Shanxi; Zhejiang had Cao Jin, later replaced by Liu Zhong; Shaanxi had Zhao Qin; Shanxi had Zhang Zhong; Henan had Lu Kun; Guangdong had Li Feng and Li Jing; Yunnan had Yang Rong; Liaodong had Gao Huai; Jiangxi had Pan Xiang; Fujian had Gao Cai; Huguang had Chen Feng; and Zeng received the edict to mine Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs fanned out: Wang Liang in Hebei, Tian Jin in the northeast, Wang Zhong in the west, Cao Jin in Zhejiang, Zhao Qin in Shaanxi, Zhang Zhong in Shanxi, Lu Kun in Henan, Li Feng and Li Jing in Guangdong, Yang Rong in Yunnan, Gao Huai in Liaodong, Pan Xiang in Jiangxi, Gao Cai in Fujian, Chen Feng in Huguang—and Zeng was ordered to mine Shandong.

sentences.zh: 通都大邑皆有稅監，兩淮則有鹽監，廣東則有珠監，或專遣，或兼攝。

translations.literal: Every great city had tax supervisors; Liang-Huai had salt supervisors; Guangdong had pearl supervisors—some specially dispatched, some holding several posts.
translations.idiomatic: Major cities gained tax supervisors; Liang-Huai had salt monitors; Guangdong had pearl monitors—some dedicated, some doubled up.

sentences.zh: 大珰小監縱橫繹騷，吸髓飲血，以供進奉。

translations.literal: Great and small eunuchs ran wild, sucking marrow and drinking blood to supply the court.
translations.idiomatic: Senior and junior eunuchs ran riot, bleeding the realm to feed the palace.

sentences.zh: 大率入公帑者不及什一，而天下蕭然，生靈塗炭矣。

translations.literal: As a rule not one in ten reached the public treasury, and the realm was desolate; the living were in torment.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps one part in ten reached the treasury; the land was ruined and the people crushed.

sentences.zh: 其最橫者增及陳奉、高淮。

translations.literal: The most overbearing were Zeng, Chen Feng, and Gao Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The worst were Zeng, Chen Feng, and Gao Huai.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，增始至山東，即劾福山知縣韋國賢，帝為逮問削職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when Zeng first reached Shandong, he at once impeached Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian; the emperor had him arrested, tried, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Zeng reached Shandong and immediately impeached Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian, who was arrested and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 益都知縣吳宗堯抗增，被陷幾死詔獄。

translations.literal: Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao resisted Zeng and was nearly killed in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao defied Zeng and nearly died in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 巡撫尹應元奏增二十大罪，亦罰俸。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Yin Yingyuan memorialized Zeng's twenty great crimes and was also fined a year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Yin Yingyuan listed twenty crimes against Zeng and was fined a year's salary himself.

sentences.zh: 已，復命增兼徵山東店稅，與臨清稅監馬堂相爭。

translations.literal: Later the emperor again ordered Zeng to levy Shandong shop taxes in addition, contending with the Linqing tax supervisor Ma Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zeng was also ordered to levy Shandong shop taxes, clashing with Linqing supervisor Ma Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝為和解，使堂稅臨清，增稅東昌。

translations.literal: The emperor mediated: Tang taxed Linqing and Zeng taxed Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor split them: Tang took Linqing, Zeng took Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 增益肆無忌，其黨內閣中書程守訓、中軍官仝治等，自江南北至浙江，大作奸弊。

translations.literal: Zeng grew still more unrestrained; his men, Grand Secretariat clerk Cheng Shouxun and military officer Tong Zhi and others, from south of the Yangtze to Zhejiang committed great wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng grew bolder; his men Cheng Shouxun and Tong Zhi committed outrages from the Yangtze to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 稱奉密旨搜金寶，募人告密。

translations.literal: They claimed a secret edict to search for gold and treasures and recruited informers.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed secret orders to hunt gold and gems and recruited informers.

sentences.zh: 誣大商巨室藏違禁物，所破滅什伯家，殺人莫敢問。

translations.literal: They falsely charged great merchants with hoarding forbidden goods; they ruined scores of households and killed without anyone daring to ask.
translations.idiomatic: They accused great merchants of hoarding contraband, ruined dozens of families, and killed with impunity.

sentences.zh: 御史劉曰梧具以狀聞，鹽務少監魯保亦奏守訓等阻塞鹽課，帝俱弗省。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Yuewu reported the facts in full; salt supervisor Lu Bao also memorialized that Shouxun and others blocked salt revenue; the emperor paid no heed to either.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Yuewu reported all; salt supervisor Lu Bao said Shouxun blocked salt revenue—the emperor ignored both.

sentences.zh: 久之，鳳陽巡撫李三才劾守訓奸贓。

translations.literal: After a long time, Fengyang grand coordinator Li Sancai impeached Shouxun for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Fengyang grand coordinator Li Sancai impeached Shouxun for graft.

sentences.zh: 增懼，因搜得守訓違禁珍寶及賕銀四十餘萬，聞於朝。

translations.literal: Zeng was afraid; in a search he found forbidden treasures and more than four hundred thousand in bribe silver belonging to Shouxun and reported it to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, afraid, searched Shouxun's stash, found forbidden treasures and four hundred thousand in bribes, and reported up.

sentences.zh: 命械入京鞫治，乃論死。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him shackled and brought to the capital for trial; he was then sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun was shackled to the capital, tried, and executed.

sentences.zh: 而增肆惡山東者十年，至三十三年始死。

translations.literal: Yet Zeng ran wild in Shandong for ten years and only died in the thirty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng terrorized Shandong for ten years and died only in year thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 陳奉，御馬監奉御也。

translations.literal: Chen Feng was an attendant of the Imperial Horse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Feng was an attendant of the Imperial Horse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十七年二月命徵荊州店稅，兼采興國州礦洞丹砂及錢廠鼓鑄事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year of Wanli he was ordered to levy Jingzhou shop taxes and also to take charge of mining cinnabar at Xingguo prefecture and minting at the coin works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 27 he was ordered to levy Jingzhou shop taxes and mine cinnabar at Xingguo while running the mint.

sentences.zh: 奉兼領數使，恣行威虐。

translations.literal: Feng held several commissions at once and acted with wanton cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Feng held several posts at once and ruled by terror.

sentences.zh: 每托巡歷，鞭笞官吏，剽劫行旅。

translations.literal: Whenever he claimed to be on inspection tour he flogged officials and robbed travelers.
translations.idiomatic: On "inspection tours" he flogged officials and robbed travelers.

sentences.zh: 商民恨刺骨，伺奉自武昌抵荊州，聚數千人噪於塗，競擲瓦石擊之。

translations.literal: Merchants hated him to the bone; when Feng went from Wuchang to Jingzhou, thousands gathered on the road shouting and pelting him with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants hated him; thousands stoned him on the road from Wuchang to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 奉走免，遂誣襄陽知府李商井黃州知府趙文煒、荊州推官華鈺、荊門知州高則巽、黃州經歷車任重等煽亂。

translations.literal: Feng escaped; he then falsely charged Xiangyang prefect Li Shangjing, Huangzhou prefect Zhao Wenwei, Jingzhou judge Hua Yu, Jingmen prefect Gao Zexun, and Huangzhou registrar Che Wuzhong with inciting riot.
translations.idiomatic: Feng escaped and framed Xiangyang prefect Li Shangjing, Huangzhou prefect Zhao Wenwei, Jingzhou judge Hua Yu, Jingmen prefect Gao Zexun, and Huangzhou registrar Che Wuzhong for inciting riot.

sentences.zh: 帝為逮鈺、任重，而謫商井等官。

translations.literal: The emperor had Yu and Wuzhong arrested while demoting Shangjing and the other officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arrested Yu and Wuzhong and demoted the others.

sentences.zh: 興國州奸人漆有光，訐居民徐鼎等掘唐相李林甫妻楊氏墓，得黃金巨萬。

translations.literal: A Xingguo scoundrel, Qi Youguang, reported that residents Xu Ding and others had dug the tomb of Tang chancellor Li Linfu's wife Lady Yang and obtained vast gold.
translations.idiomatic: A Xingguo scoundrel, Qi Youguang, claimed locals had dug Li Linfu's wife's tomb for vast gold.

sentences.zh: 騰驤衛百戶仇世亨奏之，帝命奉括進內庫。

translations.literal: Tengxiang Guard centurion Qiu Shixiang memorialized it; the emperor ordered Feng to seize it all for the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion Qiu Shixiang reported it; the emperor ordered Feng to seize everything for the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 奉因毒拷責償，且悉發境內諸墓。

translations.literal: Feng therefore tortured victims for repayment and opened every tomb in the region.
translations.idiomatic: Feng tortured for repayment and opened every tomb in the region.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史王立賢言所掘墓乃元呂文德妻，非林甫妻。

translations.literal: Regional censor Wang Lixian said the tomb dug was that of Yuan Lü Wende's wife, not Li Linfu's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Regional censor Wang Lixian said the tomb was Yuan minister Lü Wende's wife, not Li Linfu's.

sentences.zh: 奸人訐奏，語多不仇，請罷不治，而停他處開掘，不報。

translations.literal: The scoundrel's impeachment contained many contradictions; he asked that prosecution cease and other digging stop; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The informer's tale contradicted itself; Wang asked to stop digging—no reply.

sentences.zh: 二十八年十二月，武昌民變。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-eighth year the people of Wuchang rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year twenty-eight Wuchang rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 南京吏部主事吳中明奏言：「奉嚇詐官民，僭稱千歲。

translations.literal: Nanjing Ministry of Personnel director Wu Zhongming memorialized: "Feng terrorizes officials and people and presumptuously calls himself 'a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Ministry director Wu Zhongming wrote: "Feng terrorizes the realm and calls himself 'a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 其黨至直入民家，奸淫婦女，或掠入稅監署中。

translations.literal: His men even entered private homes, raped women, or seized them into the tax depot.
translations.idiomatic: His men entered homes, raped women, or dragged them into the tax depot.

sentences.zh: 王生之女、沈生之妻，皆被逼辱。

translations.literal: A Mr. Wang's daughter and a Mr. Shen's wife were both forced and shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Wang's daughter and Mr. Shen's wife were among those violated.

sentences.zh: 以致士民公憤，萬餘人甘與奉同死，撫按三司護之數日，僅而得全。

translations.literal: So that scholars and commoners in public rage, more than ten thousand were willing to die with Feng; the grand coordinator and the three offices protected him for days before he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand commoners were ready to die with Feng; officials shielded him for days before he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 而巡撫支可大，曲為蒙蔽。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Coordinator Zhi Kedai whitewashed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhi Kedai covered for him.

sentences.zh: 天下禍亂，將何所底！」

translations.literal: Where will the realm's calamities end!'
translations.idiomatic: Where will the realm's disasters end!'

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫亦言：「陳奉入楚，始而武昌一變，繼之漢口、黃州、襄陽、武昌、寶慶、德安、湘潭等處，變經十起，幾成大亂。

translations.literal: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan also said: "Since Feng entered Chu, first came the Wuchang disturbance, then Hankou, Huangzhou, Xiangyang, Wuchang again, Baqing, Dean, Xiangtan—ten outbreaks, nearly great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan wrote: "Since Feng entered Chu there have been ten uprisings from Wuchang to Xiangtan—near rebellion.

sentences.zh: 立乞撤回，以收楚民之心。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be recalled to win back the hearts of the Chu people.
translations.idiomatic: Recall him to win back the people of Chu."

sentences.zh: 帝皆置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor set it all aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored everything.

sentences.zh: 奉復使人開谷城礦，不獲，脅其庫金，為縣所逐。

translations.literal: Feng again sent men to open a mine at Gucheng; when nothing was found he extorted the county treasury and was driven out by the county.
translations.idiomatic: Feng opened a mine at Gucheng, found nothing, extorted the county treasury, and was driven out.

sentences.zh: 武昌兵備僉事馮應京劾奉十大罪，奉隨誣奏，降應京雜職。

translations.literal: Wuchang military intendant Feng Yingjing impeached Feng's ten great crimes; Feng at once slandered him in a memorial and Yingjing was demoted to miscellaneous rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang intendant Feng Yingjing impeached Feng's ten crimes; Feng slandered him back and Yingjing was demoted.

sentences.zh: 奉又開棗陽礦，知縣王之翰以顯陵近，執不可。

translations.literal: Feng again opened a mine at Zaoyang; magistrate Wang Zhihan, because it was near the imperial tomb, held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Feng opened a Zaoyang mine; magistrate Wang Zhihan refused because it was near the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 奉劾之翰及襄陽通判邸宅、推官何棟如，緹騎逮訊，並追逮應京。

translations.literal: Feng impeached Zhihan and Xiangyang vice prefect Qiu Zhai and judge He Dongru; brocade-clad guards arrested them for interrogation and also pursued Yingjing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng impeached Zhihan, Qiu Zhai, and He Dongru; guards arrested them and pursued Yingjing.

sentences.zh: 應京素有惠政，民號哭送之。

translations.literal: Yingjing had long had benevolent government; the people wept and saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing had ruled with kindness; the people wept as he was taken away.

sentences.zh: 奉又榜列應京罪狀於衢。

translations.literal: Feng also posted Yingjing's crimes in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Feng posted Yingjing's alleged crimes in the streets.

sentences.zh: 民切齒恨，復相聚圍奉署，誓必殺奉。

translations.literal: The people gnashed their teeth in hatred and again gathered to surround Feng's depot, swearing to kill Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The people surrounded Feng's depot, swearing to kill him.

sentences.zh: 奉逃匿楚王府，眾乃投奉黨耿文登等十六人於江，以巡撫可大護奉，焚其轅門。

translations.literal: Feng fled into the Chu princely mansion; the crowd then threw sixteen of Feng's men including Geng Wendeng into the river; because Grand Coordinator Kedai protected Feng, they burned his yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: Feng fled to the Chu princely mansion; the crowd drowned sixteen of his men and burned Kedai's gate because he shielded Feng.

sentences.zh: 事聞，一貫及給事中姚文蔚等請撤奉，不報。

translations.literal: When word reached court, Yiguan and supervising secretary Yao Wenwei and others asked that Feng be withdrawn; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan and Yao Wenwei asked to withdraw Feng—no reply.

sentences.zh: 而御馬監監丞李道方督理湖口船稅，亦奏奉水沮商舟，陸截販賈，徵三解一，病國剝民。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Imperial Horse Directorate director Li Daofang, supervising Hukou boat taxes, also memorialized that Feng on water blocked merchant boats and on land intercepted peddlers, levying three parts and releasing one—harming the state and stripping the people.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Horse director Li Daofang also said Feng blocked boats on the river and peddlers on land, taking three parts and releasing one.

sentences.zh: 帝始召奉歸，而用一貫請，革可大職。

translations.literal: The emperor at last recalled Feng and, following Yiguan's request, stripped Kedai of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally recalled Feng and, at Yiguan's request, stripped Kedai of office.

sentences.zh: 奉在湖廣二年，慘毒備至。

translations.literal: Feng had been in Huguang two years, and his cruelty reached every extreme.
translations.idiomatic: For two years in Huguang, Feng's cruelty knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 及去，金寶財物巨萬計，可大懼為民所掠，多與徒衛，導之出疆，楚民無不毒恨者。

translations.literal: When he left, gold, jewels, and goods numbered in the tens of thousands; Kedai feared the people would loot them and gave many to his followers and guards to escort them out of the province; the people of Chu all hated him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, his loot ran to tens of thousands; Kedai feared the mob and sent guards to escort it out—Chu hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 奉至京師，給事中陳維春、郭如星復極言其罪。

translations.literal: When Feng reached the capital, supervising secretaries Chen Weichun and Guo Ruxing again spoke to the limit of his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital, Chen Weichun and Guo Ruxing again denounced his crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，降二人雜職。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and demoted the two to miscellaneous rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and demoted both men.

sentences.zh: 三十二年始釋應京歸，之翰卒瘐死。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Yingjing was released to return home; Zhihan died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-two Yingjing was freed; Zhihan died in prison.

sentences.zh: 當奉劾商井等時，臨清民亦噪而逐馬堂。

translations.literal: When Feng had impeached Shangjing and others, the people of Linqing also rioted and drove out Ma Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng impeached Shangjing, Linqing rioted and drove out Ma Tang.

sentences.zh: 馬堂者，天津稅監也，兼轄臨清。

translations.literal: Ma Tang was the Tianjin tax supervisor and also governed Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tang was Tianjin tax supervisor with authority over Linqing.

sentences.zh: 始至，諸亡命從者數百人，白晝手鋃鐺奪人產，抗者輒以違禁罪之。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, several hundred desperadoes followed him; by day they wore manacles and seized people's property, and those who resisted were charged with forbidden offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of ruffians followed him; by day they seized property in shackles and charged resisters with contraband crimes.

sentences.zh: 僮告主者，畀以十之三，中人之家破者大半，遠近為罷市。

translations.literal: If a servant informed on his master, he was given three-tenths; middle households were ruined in more than half, and markets far and near closed.
translations.idiomatic: Informers got a tenth; half the middling households were ruined and markets shut down.

sentences.zh: 州民萬餘縱火焚堂署，斃其黨三十七人，皆黥臂諸偷也。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand prefecture people set fire to Tang's depot and killed thirty-seven of his men—all were tattooed-arm thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand townspeople burned Tang's depot and killed thirty-seven tattooed thieves in his service.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔捕首惡，株連甚眾。

translations.literal: When word reached court, an edict ordered the ringleaders seized; many were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the ringleaders seized and implicated many.

sentences.zh: 有王朝佐者，素仗義，慨然出曰：「首難者，我也。」

translations.literal: One Wang Chaozuo, who had long upheld righteousness, came forward boldly and said: "I am the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chaozuo, a man of principle, stepped forward: "I am the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，神色不變。

translations.literal: At execution his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: At execution his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 知府李士登恤其母妻，臨清民立祠以祀。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Shideng comforted his mother and wife; the people of Linqing built a shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Shideng cared for his family; Linqing built him a shrine.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，堂擅往揚州，巡鹽御史徐縉芳劾其九罪，不問。

translations.literal: More than ten years later Tang went without permission to Yangzhou; salt censor Xu Jifang impeached his nine crimes; no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later Tang went to Yangzhou; salt censor Xu Jifang impeached nine crimes—ignored.

sentences.zh: 高淮，尚膳監監丞也。

translations.literal: Gao Huai was a director of the Imperial Catering Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huai was a director of the Imperial Catering Directorate.

sentences.zh: 神宗寵愛諸稅監，自大學士趙誌臯、沈一貫而下，廷臣諫者不下百餘疏，悉寢不報。

translations.literal: The Shenzong emperor favored the tax supervisors; from Chief Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan down, more than a hundred court memorials of remonstrance were all shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong favored tax eunuchs; over a hundred memorials from Zhao Zhigao, Shen Yiguan, and others were shelved.

sentences.zh: 而諸稅監有所糾劾，朝上夕下，輒加重譴。

translations.literal: Yet when tax supervisors impeached someone, memorials arrived evening and morning and punishments were always heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When tax eunuchs impeached someone, punishment followed at once.

sentences.zh: 以故諸稅監益驕，而淮及梁永尤甚。

translations.literal: Thus the tax supervisors grew still more arrogant, and Huai and Liang Yong were worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: Tax eunuchs grew bolder; Huai and Liang Yong were the worst.

sentences.zh: 淮與陳奉同時采礦徵稅遼東。

translations.literal: Huai and Chen Feng at the same time mined and levied taxes in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai mined and taxed Liaodong alongside Chen Feng.

sentences.zh: 委官廖國泰，虐民激變，淮誣系諸生數十人。

translations.literal: His appointed official Liao Guotai abused the people and provoked revolt; Huai falsely imprisoned dozens of students.
translations.idiomatic: His agent Liao Guotai provoked revolt; Huai jailed dozens of students on false charges.

sentences.zh: 巡按楊宏科救之，不報。

translations.literal: Regional censor Yang Hongke rescued them; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Regional censor Yang Hongke intervened—ignored.

sentences.zh: 參隨楊永恩婪賄事發，奉旨會勘，卒不問。

translations.literal: Attendant Yang Yong'en's greedy bribery was exposed; an edict ordered joint investigation; in the end no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Yang Yong'en's bribery was exposed; joint investigation was ordered—then dropped.

sentences.zh: 淮又惡遼東總兵馬林不為己下，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Huai also hated Liaodong regional commander Ma Lin for not submitting to him and impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai hated commander Ma Lin for not bowing to him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 給事中候先春疏救，遂戍林而謫先春雜職。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Hou Xianchun memorialized in his defense; Lin was exiled and Xianchun demoted to miscellaneous rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xianchun defended Ma Lin; Lin was exiled and Hou demoted.

sentences.zh: 巡按何爾健與淮互訐奏，淮遣人邀於路，責其奏事人，錮之獄，匿疏不以聞。

translations.literal: Regional censor He Erjian and Huai impeached each other in memorials; Huai sent men to intercept him on the road, blamed his memorial clerk, imprisoned him, and hid the memorial without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: He Erjian and Huai traded impeachments; Huai intercepted He on the road, jailed his clerk, and suppressed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 又請復遼東馬市，巡撫趙楫力爭，始得寢。

translations.literal: He also asked to restore the Liaodong horse market; Grand Coordinator Zhao Ji fought hard before it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reopen the Liaodong horse market; Zhao Ji blocked it.

sentences.zh: 三十一年夏，淮率家丁三百餘，張飛虎幟，金鼓震天，聲言欲入大內謁帝，潛住廣渠門外。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-first year Huai led more than three hundred household retainers with Flying Tiger banners; drums and gongs shook heaven; he claimed he would enter the inner palace to see the emperor and secretly stayed outside Guangqu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year thirty-one Huai camped three hundred armed retainers outside Guangqu Gate claiming he would enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中田大益、孫善繼、姚文蔚等言：「淮搜括士民，取金至數十萬，招納諸亡命降人，意欲何為？」

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Tian Dayi, Sun Shanji, Yao Wenwei, and others said: "Huai extorts from scholars and commoners gold to the tens of thousands, recruits desperadoes and surrendered tribesmen—what does he intend?
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dayi, Sun Shanji, and Yao Wenwei asked what Huai meant by extorting hundreds of thousands and recruiting desperadoes.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李戴、刑部尚書蕭大亨皆劾淮擅離信地，挾兵潛住京師，乃數百年未有之事。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Dai and Minister of Justice Xiao Daheng both impeached Huai for leaving his post without permission and bringing troops to lurk in the capital—a thing unheard of in centuries.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai and Xiao Daheng impeached him for bringing armed men to the capital—unheard of in centuries.

sentences.zh: 御史袁九臯、劉四科、孔貞一，給事中梁有年等，各疏劾淮，不報。

translations.literal: Censors Yuan Jiugao, Liu Sike, Kong Zhenyi, supervising secretary Liang Younian, and others each memorialized against Huai; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Yuan Jiugao, Liu Sike, Kong Zhenyi, and Liang Younian memorialized—no reply.

sentences.zh: 巡撫楫劾淮罪惡萬端，且無故打死指揮張汝立，亦不報。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ji impeached Huai's countless crimes and his killing without cause of commander Zhang Ruli; also no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ji listed his crimes including killing commander Zhang Ruli—ignored.

sentences.zh: 淮因上疏自稱鎮守協同關務，兵部奏其妄。

translations.literal: Huai therefore memorialized calling himself coordinator of joint frontier duties; the Ministry of War reported this as false.
translations.idiomatic: Huai claimed the title of frontier coordinator; the Ministry of War called it false.

sentences.zh: 帝心護淮，謬曰：「朕固命之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor's heart protected Huai and he wrongly said: "We ordered it so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shielded him: "I ordered it myself."

sentences.zh: 淮自是益募死士，時時出塞射獵，髮黃票龍旗，走朝鮮索冠珠、貂馬，數與邊將爭功，山海關內外咸被其毒。

translations.literal: From this Huai recruited dead soldiers all the more, often went beyond the pass to hunt, flew yellow tickets and dragon banners, went to Korea demanding crown pearls and sable horses, repeatedly quarreled with frontier generals over merit, and inside and outside Shanhai Pass all suffered his poison.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited braves, hunted beyond the pass under dragon banners, extorted Korea for pearls and horses, fought generals for credit, and poisoned the whole northeast.

sentences.zh: 又扣除軍士月糧。

translations.literal: He also deducted soldiers' monthly grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut soldiers' monthly rations.

sentences.zh: 三十六年四月，前屯衛軍甲而噪，誓食淮肉。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-sixth year the troops of Qiantun Guard mutinied in armor, swearing to eat Huai's flesh.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year thirty-six Qiantun troops mutinied, vowing to eat Huai alive.

sentences.zh: 六月，錦州、松山軍復變。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the troops of Jinzhou and Songshan mutinied again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jinzhou and Songshan troops mutinied again.

sentences.zh: 淮懼內奔，誣同知王邦才、參將李獲陽逐殺欽使，劫奪御用錢糧。

translations.literal: Huai fled inward in fear, falsely charging Vice Commissioner Wang Bangcai and Regional Commander Li Huoyang with driving off and killing imperial envoys and robbing imperial funds.
translations.idiomatic: Huai fled inward and framed Wang Bangcai and Li Huoyang for killing envoys and robbing imperial funds.

sentences.zh: 二人皆逮問，邊民益嘩。

translations.literal: Both were arrested for trial and frontier people grew more clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: Both were arrested and the frontier erupted.

sentences.zh: 薊遼總督蹇達再疏暴淮罪，乃召歸，而以通灣稅監張曄兼領其事。

translations.literal: Jiliao supreme commander Qian Da again memorialized exposing Huai's crimes; he was then recalled, and Tongwan tax supervisor Zhang Ye was ordered to take charge as well.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Qian Da exposed Huai's crimes; he was recalled and Zhang Ye took over.

sentences.zh: 獲陽竟死獄中，邦才至四十一年乃釋。

translations.literal: Huoyang died in prison; Bangcai was not released until the forty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: Huoyang died in prison; Bangcai was freed only in year forty-one.

sentences.zh: 梁永，御馬監監丞也。

translations.literal: Liang Yong was a director of the Imperial Horse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yong was a director of the Imperial Horse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十七年二月命往陜西征收名馬貨物。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year of Wanli he was ordered to Shaanxi to levy famous horses and goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 27 he was sent to Shaanxi to levy horses and goods.

sentences.zh: 稅監故不典兵，永獨畜馬五百匹，招致亡命，用千戶樂綱出入邊塞。

translations.literal: Tax supervisors by tradition did not command troops; Yong alone kept five hundred horses and recruited desperadoes, using centurion Yue Gang to go in and out of the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Tax eunuchs did not command troops; Yong kept five hundred horses and used centurion Yue Gang on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 富平知縣王正誌發其奸，並劾礦監趙欽。

translations.literal: Fuping magistrate Wang Zhengzhi exposed his wickedness and also impeached mining supervisor Zhao Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fuping magistrate Wang Zhengzhi exposed Yong and impeached mining supervisor Zhao Qin.

sentences.zh: 詔逮正誌，瘐死詔獄中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhengzhi arrested; he died of illness in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi was arrested and died in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 渭南知縣徐斗牛，廉吏也。

translations.literal: Weinan magistrate Xu Douniu was an honest official.
translations.idiomatic: Weinan magistrate Xu Douniu was incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 永責賂，箠斃縣吏卒，斗牛憤恨自縊死。

translations.literal: Yong demanded bribes, beat county clerks and runners to death; Douniu in rage hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yong demanded bribes and beat clerks to death; Douniu hanged himself in rage.

sentences.zh: 巡撫賈待問奏之，帝顧使永會勘。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Jia Daiwen memorialized it; the emperor merely sent Yong to joint investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Jia Daiwen reported it; the emperor sent Yong to investigate himself.

sentences.zh: 永反劾西安同知宋賢，並劾待問有私，請皆勘。

translations.literal: Yong in turn impeached Xi'an vice commissioner Song Xian and charged Daiwen with favoritism, asking that all be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Yong impeached Song Xian and accused Daiwen of bias, demanding investigation of all.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，而宥待問。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed but pardoned Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed but spared Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 永又請兼鎮守職銜。

translations.literal: Yong also asked for a concurrent frontier commander's title.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also asked for a frontier commander's title.

sentences.zh: 又請率兵巡花馬池、慶陽諸鹽池，徵其課。

translations.literal: He also asked to lead troops on inspection of Huama Pool, Qingyang, and other salt pans and levy their dues.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to lead troops to inspect salt pans at Huama Pool and Qingyang and levy dues.

sentences.zh: 緣是帥諸亡命，具旌蓋鼓吹，巡行陜地。

translations.literal: Thus he led desperadoes with banners, canopies, drums, and pipes touring Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Shaanxi with banners, drums, and a host of ruffians.

sentences.zh: 盡發歷代陵寢，搜摸金玉，旁行劫掠。

translations.literal: He opened tombs of every dynasty, searched for gold and jade, and plundered on every side.
translations.idiomatic: He opened dynastic tombs for gold and jade and plundered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 所至，邑令皆逃。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, county magistrates all fled.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates fled wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 杖死縣丞鄭思顏、指揮劉應聘、諸生李洪遠等。

translations.literal: He beat to death county assistant Zheng Siyan, commander Liu Yingpin, student Li Hongyuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He beat to death Zheng Siyan, Liu Yingpin, Li Hongyuan, and others.

sentences.zh: 縱樂綱等肆為淫掠，私宮良家子數十人。

translations.literal: He let Yue Gang and others run wild in rape and plunder and privately seized dozens of respectable families' sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Gang and others raped and plundered; Yong seized dozens of respectable sons.

sentences.zh: 稅額外增耗數倍，藍田等七關歲得十萬。

translations.literal: Tax quotas were increased several times beyond the norm; the seven passes of Lantian and elsewhere yielded a hundred thousand a year.
translations.idiomatic: He multiplied tax quotas; seven Lantian passes alone yielded a hundred thousand a year.

sentences.zh: 復用奸人胡奉言，索咸陽冰片五十斤、羊毛一萬斤、麝香二十斤。

translations.literal: He again used the scoundrel Hu Fengyan to demand fifty jin of Xianyang borneol, ten thousand jin of wool, and twenty jin of musk.
translations.idiomatic: He used Hu Fengyan to demand fifty jin of borneol, ten thousand jin of wool, and twenty jin of musk.

sentences.zh: 知縣宋時際怒，勿予。

translations.literal: Magistrate Song Shiji was angry and would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Song Shiji refused.

sentences.zh: 咸寧人道行遇盜，跡之，稅使役也，知縣滿朝薦捕得之。

translations.literal: A Xianning traveler met bandits; tracking them, they were tax depot runners; magistrate Man Chaojian arrested them.
translations.idiomatic: A Xianning traveler was robbed by tax depot runners; magistrate Man Chaojian caught them.

sentences.zh: 永誣時際、朝薦劫稅銀，帝命逮時際，而以朝薦到官未久，鐫秩一級。

translations.literal: Yong falsely charged Shiji and Chaojian with robbing tax silver; the emperor ordered Shiji arrested while Chaojian, having just taken office, was cut one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yong charged them with robbing tax silver; Shiji was ordered arrested and Chaojian cut one rank.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫顧其志盡發其奸，且言秦民萬眾，共圖殺永。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Gu Qizhi fully exposed his crimes and said a hundred thousand Qin people jointly plotted to kill Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gu Qizhi exposed Yong and said a hundred thousand Qin people plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈鯉、朱賡請械永歸，以安眾心。

translations.literal: Chief grand secretaries Shen Li and Zhu Geng asked that Yong be shackled and returned to calm hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li and Zhu Geng asked that Yong be shackled and returned.

sentences.zh: 帝悉置不報，而釋時際勿逮，復朝薦官。

translations.literal: The emperor set it all aside but released Shiji from arrest and restored Chaojian's office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them but spared Shiji and restored Chaojian.

sentences.zh: 會御史余懋衡方按陜西，永懼，使綱鴆懋衡幾死。

translations.literal: When censor Yu Maohang was inspecting Shaanxi, Yong feared him and had Gang poison him nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Maohang inspected Shaanxi; Yong had Gang poison him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 訟於朝，言官攻永者數十疏，永部下諸亡命乃稍稍散。

translations.literal: The case went to court; dozens of memorials attacked Yong; Yong's desperado followers then gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The case reached court; dozens attacked Yong; his ruffians dispersed.

sentences.zh: 其渠魁王九功、石君章等賫重寶，輜軿盈路，詐為上供物，持劍戟弓弩，結陣以行。

translations.literal: Ringleaders Wang Jiugong, Shi Junzhang, and others carried heavy treasures; carts filled the road, pretending to be tribute goods, bearing swords, halberds, and crossbows, marching in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Ringleaders Wang Jiugong and Shi Junzhang marched with treasure carts disguised as tribute, armed with swords and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 而永所遣人解馬匹者，已乘郵傳先發。

translations.literal: Men Yong had sent to deliver horses had already taken the post roads and left first.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's horse couriers had already left by post road.

sentences.zh: 九功等急馳，欲追及與同出關。

translations.literal: Jiugong and the others galloped hard, wishing to catch up and leave the pass together.
translations.idiomatic: Jiugong galloped to catch the horse train and leave the pass together.

sentences.zh: 朝薦疑其盜，見九功等後至無驗，邏兵與格鬥，追至渭南，殺數人，盡奪其裝。

translations.literal: Chaojian suspected them as robbers; seeing Jiugong arrive later without proof, he sent troops to fight; pursuing to Weinan they killed several and seized all their goods.
translations.idiomatic: Chaojian thought them robbers, fought them at Weinan, killed several, and seized their goods.

sentences.zh: 御史懋衡以捕盜殺傷聞。

translations.literal: Censor Maohang reported capturing robbers with casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Maohang reported killing robbers in the fight.

sentences.zh: 永大窘，聽樂綱謀，使人系疏發中馳奏：「九功等各貢名馬、金珠、睛綠諸寶物，而咸寧知縣朝薦承余御史指，伏兵渭南遮劫之，臠君章等，誣以盜。」
