translations.literal: Yong was greatly embarrassed and listened to Yue Gang's plot, having a man tie a memorial in his hair and gallop to report: "Jiugong and each presented famous horses, gold, pearls, bright green jewels, and other treasures, while Xianning magistrate Chaojian, at censor Yu's direction, ambushed at Weinan and robbed them, dismembering Junzhang and calling them robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had a rider report that Chaojian, at Yu Maohang's direction, ambushed tribute bearers at Weinan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「御史鴆無恙，而朝薦代為報復，且劫貢物。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "The censor was poisoned yet unharmed, while Chaojian avenged him and moreover robbed tribute goods."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged that Chaojian had robbed tribute while the poisoned censor lived.

sentences.zh: 敕逮朝薦，而令撫按護永等還京。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chaojian arrested while the grand coordinator and regional inspector were told to escort Yong and others back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chaojian was arrested; Yong was escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十四年事也。

translations.literal: This was in the thirty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in year thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 是年，楊榮為雲南人所殺。

translations.literal: That year Yang Rong was killed by the people of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Rong was killed in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 初，榮妄奏阿瓦、猛密諸番願內屬，其地有寶井，可歲益數十萬，願賜敕領其事。

translations.literal: Earlier Rong had falsely memorialized that Ava, Mengmi, and other tribes wished to submit and that their land had treasure wells yielding hundreds of thousands yearly, asking an edict to lead the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had falsely claimed Ava and Mengmi wished to submit and that treasure wells would yield hundreds of thousands yearly.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而榮所進不得什一，乃誣知府熊鐸侵匿，下法司。

translations.literal: Later what Rong presented did not reach one-tenth; he then falsely charged prefect Xiong Duo with concealment and sent him to the law courts.
translations.idiomatic: His yield was less than a tenth; he charged prefect Xiong Duo with concealment.

sentences.zh: 又請詔麗江土知府木增獻地聽開采。

translations.literal: He also asked an edict that Lijiang native prefect Mu Zeng cede land for mining.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Mu Zeng of Lijiang to cede land for mining.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史宋興祖言：「太祖令木氏世守茲土，限石門以絕西域，守鐵橋以斷土蕃，奈何自撤藩蔽，生遠人心。」

translations.literal: Regional censor Song Xingzu said: "Taizu ordered the Mu clan to guard this land forever, using Stone Gate to block the Western Regions and Iron Bridge to cut off the Tibetan tribes—how can We ourselves remove the frontier barrier and stir distant hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Song Xingzu said Taizu had made the Mu clan guard the frontier—why remove the barrier and stir distant tribes?

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply.

sentences.zh: 榮由是愈怙寵，誣劾尋甸知府蔡如川、趙州知州甘學書，皆下詔獄。

translations.literal: Rong therefore grew still more arrogant in favor, falsely impeaching Xundian prefect Cai Ruchuan and Zhao prefect Gan Xueshu; both were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Rong grew bolder, impeaching Xundian prefect Cai Ruchuan and Zhao prefect Gan Xueshu.

sentences.zh: 已，又誣劾雲南知府周鐸，下法司提問。

translations.literal: Later he also falsely impeached Yunnan prefect Zhou Duo and sent him to the law courts for trial.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Yunnan prefect Zhou Duo.

sentences.zh: 百姓恨榮入骨，相率燔稅廠，殺委官張安民。

translations.literal: The people hated Rong to the marrow; they together burned the tax depot and killed appointed official Zhang Anmin.
translations.idiomatic: The people burned the tax depot and killed Zhang Anmin.

sentences.zh: 榮弗悛，恣行威虐，杖斃數千人。

translations.literal: Rong did not repent but acted with wanton cruelty and beat thousands to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong beat thousands to death without remorse.

sentences.zh: 至是怒指揮使樊高明後期，榜掠絕觔，枷以示眾。

translations.literal: At this he was angry that commander Fan Gaoming was late and flogged him until he stopped eating, putting him in the cangue for display.
translations.idiomatic: He flogged late commander Fan Gaoming until he could not eat and cangued him for display.

sentences.zh: 又以求馬不獲，系指揮使賀瑞鳳，且言將盡捕六衛官。

translations.literal: Again, for not obtaining horses, he imprisoned commander He Ruifeng and said he would arrest all officers of the six guards.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned He Ruifeng for failing to deliver horses and threatened all six guards.

sentences.zh: 於是指揮賀世勛、韓光大等率冤民萬人焚榮第，殺之，投火中，並殺其黨二百餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon commanders He Shixun, Han Guangda, and others led ten thousand wronged people to burn Rong's residence, kill him, and throw him in the fire, also killing more than two hundred of his men.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders He Shixun and Han Guangda led ten thousand people to burn Rong's house and kill him and two hundred of his men.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝為不食者數日，欲逮問守土官。

translations.literal: When word reached court the emperor did not eat for several days and wished to arrest and try the local officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fasted for days and wanted to punish local officials.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈鯉揭爭，且密屬太監陳矩剖示。

translations.literal: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Li argued forcefully and secretly had eunuch Chen Ju explain.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li argued and had eunuch Chen Ju explain privately.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止誅世勛等，而用巡撫陳用賓議，令四川稅使丘乘雲兼攝雲南事。

translations.literal: The emperor then only executed Shixun and others and followed Grand Coordinator Chen Yongbin's plan, ordering Sichuan tax envoy Qiu Chengyun to take charge of Yunnan affairs as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Shixun and had Sichuan tax envoy Qiu Chengyun take Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝所遣中官，無不播虐逞凶者。

translations.literal: At that time every eunuch the emperor dispatched spread cruelty and flaunted violence.
translations.idiomatic: Every eunuch the emperor sent spread cruelty.

sentences.zh: 湖口稅監李道劾降九江府經歷樊圃充，又劾逮南康知府吳寶秀、星子知縣吳一元，降臨江知府顧起淹。

translations.literal: Hukou tax supervisor Li Dao impeached and demoted Jiujiang prefecture registrar Fan Yuanchong, also impeached and arrested Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu and Xingzi magistrate Wu Yiyuan, and demoted Linjiang prefect Gu Qiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao demoted Fan Yuanchong, arrested Wu Baoxiu and Wu Yiyuan, and demoted Gu Qiyan.

sentences.zh: 山西稅監孫朝劾降夏縣知縣韓薰。

translations.literal: Shanxi tax supervisor Sun Chao impeached and demoted Xia county magistrate Han Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi tax supervisor Sun Chao demoted Han Xun of Xia county.

sentences.zh: 給事中程紹以救薰鐫一級，給事中李應策等復救之，遂削紹、薰職。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Cheng Shao, for rescuing Xun, was cut one rank; supervising secretaries Li Yingce and others again rescued him, and Shao and Xun were both stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shao was cut one rank for rescuing Xun; Li Yingce tried again—both Shao and Xun lost office.

sentences.zh: 巡撫魏允貞以阻撓罷去。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wei Yunzhen was dismissed for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wei Yunzhen was dismissed for obstructing the tax eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 廣東稅監李鳳劾逮鄉官通判吳應鴻等。

translations.literal: Guangdong tax supervisor Li Feng impeached and arrested country magistrate and vice prefect Wu Yinghong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng of Guangdong impeached and arrested vice prefect Wu Yinghong and others.

sentences.zh: 鳳與珠池監李敬相仇，巡按李時華恃敬援劾鳳。

translations.literal: Feng was at odds with pearl-pool supervisor Li Jing; regional censor Li Shihua relied on Jing's backing to impeach Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Feng feuded with pearl supervisor Li Jing; censor Li Shihua, backed by Jing, impeached Feng.

sentences.zh: 給事中宋一韓言鳳乾沒五千餘萬，他珍寶稱是。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Song Yihan said Feng had embezzled more than fifty thousand and other jewels in like amount.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yihan said Feng had embezzled over fifty thousand taels and comparable gems.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李戴等言鳳釀禍，致潮陽鼓噪，粵中人爭欲殺之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Dai and others said Feng brewed trouble, causing Chaoyang to riot and people in Guangdong to vie to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai said Feng had provoked riots in Chaoyang and that Cantonese wanted him dead.

sentences.zh: 帝不問。

translations.literal: The emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 而敬惡亦不減於鳳，采珠七八年，歲得珠近萬兩。

translations.literal: Yet Jing's wickedness was no less than Feng's; pearl diving ran seven or eight years, yielding nearly ten thousand taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was no better; for seven or eight years he dived pearls, yielding nearly ten thousand taels a year.

sentences.zh: 其後珠池盜起，敬乃請罷采。

translations.literal: Later pearl-pool bandits arose and Jing asked to stop diving.
translations.idiomatic: When pearl-pool bandits appeared, Jing asked to stop.

sentences.zh: 山西礦監張忠劾降夏縣知縣袁應春，又劾逮西城兵馬戴文龍。

translations.literal: Shanxi mining supervisor Zhang Zhong impeached and demoted Xia county magistrate Yuan Yingchun and also impeached and arrested Xicheng military commander Dai Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong demoted Yuan Yingchun of Xia county and arrested Dai Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 江西礦監潘相激浮梁景德鎮民變，焚燒廠房。

translations.literal: Jiangxi mining supervisor Pan Xiang provoked the people of Fuliang and Jingdezhen to revolt and burned the factory buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xiang provoked a riot in Jingdezhen and burned the factories.

sentences.zh: 饒州通判陳奇可諭散之，相反劾逮奇可。

translations.literal: Raozhou vice prefect Chen Qike persuaded them to disperse but was impeached and arrested in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qike dispersed the crowd and was arrested in turn.

sentences.zh: 相檄上饒縣勘礦洞，知縣李鴻戒邑人敢以食物市者死。

translations.literal: Xiang ordered Shangrao county to survey mine caves; magistrate Li Hong warned townspeople that selling food to him meant death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang ordered a mine survey; magistrate Li Hong forbade anyone to feed him.

sentences.zh: 相竟日饑渴，憊而歸，乃螫鴻，罷其官。

translations.literal: Xiang hungered and thirsted all day, returned exhausted, then stung Hong and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went hungry all day, returned exhausted, then ruined Li Hong and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 橫嶺礦監王虎以廣昌民變，劾降易州知州孫大祚。

translations.literal: Hengling mining supervisor Wang Hu, because of a Guangchang popular disturbance, impeached and demoted Yizhou magistrate Sun Dazuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hu blamed a Guangchang riot on Yizhou magistrate Sun Dazuo and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 蘇、杭織造太監兼管稅務孫隆激民變，遍焚諸劄委稅官家，隆急走杭州以免。

translations.literal: Suzhou and Hangzhou weaving supervisor Sun Long, who also managed tax affairs, provoked popular revolt; tax offices everywhere were burned and Long fled hastily to Hangzhou to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving supervisor Sun Long provoked riots; tax offices burned and he fled to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 福建稅監高寀薦布政使陳性學，立擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Fujian tax supervisor Gao Cai recommended Administrator Chen Xingxue and he was abruptly promoted to grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cai promoted Chen Xingxue straight to grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 居閩十餘年，廣肆毒害。

translations.literal: He remained in Min more than ten years and spread poison widely.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled Fujian over ten years with great cruelty.

sentences.zh: 四十二年四月，萬眾洶洶欲殺寀，寀率甲士二百餘人入巡撫袁一驥署，露刃劫之，令諭眾退。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the forty-second year tens of thousands surged to kill Cai; Cai led more than two hundred armored men into Grand Coordinator Yuan Yiji's yamen, bared blades and seized him, ordering him to tell the crowd to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year forty-two a mob tried to kill Cai; he seized Grand Coordinator Yuan Yiji at blade point.

sentences.zh: 復挾副使李思誠、僉事呂純如等至私署要盟，始釋一驥。

translations.literal: He again took Vice Commissioner Li Sicheng and Intendant Lü Chunru to his private yamen to force an oath before releasing Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: He held Li Sicheng and Lü Chunru hostage before releasing Yiji.

sentences.zh: 復拘同知陳豸於署者久之。

translations.literal: He again detained Vice Commissioner Chen Zhi in his yamen for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He detained Vice Commissioner Chen Zhi for a long time.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝召寀還，命出豸，而一驥由此罷。

translations.literal: When word reached court the emperor recalled Cai, ordered Chen Zhi released, and Yiji was dismissed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Cai and released Chen Zhi; Yiji was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 他若山東張曄、河南魯坤、四川丘乘雲輩，皆為民害。

translations.literal: Others such as Zhang Ye of Shandong, Lu Kun of Henan, and Qiu Chengyun of Sichuan were all harms to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ye, Lu Kun, and Qiu Chengyun likewise harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 迨帝崩，始下遺詔罷礦稅，撤諸中使還京。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, a testamentary edict at last abolished mining taxes and recalled all palace envoys to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's death a testamentary edict ended mining taxes and recalled the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 陳矩，安肅人。

translations.literal: Chen Ju was a man of Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ju was from Ansu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，為司禮秉筆太監。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he was a eunuch director of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he served as Ceremonial director.

sentences.zh: 二十六年提督東廠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was put in charge of the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six he took charge of the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 為人平恕識大體。

translations.literal: He was mild and forgiving by nature and grasped larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: He was even-tempered and saw the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔收書籍，中有侍郎呂坤所著《閨範圖說》，帝以賜鄭貴妃，妃自為序，鋟諸木。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to collect books; among them was Vice Minister Lü Kun's Illustrated Admonitions for the Inner Quarters, which the emperor had given Consort Zheng; the consort wrote her own preface and had it carved on wood.
translations.idiomatic: Collecting books for the palace, he found Lü Kun's Illustrated Admonitions for the Inner Quarters, which Consort Zheng had published with her own preface.

sentences.zh: 時國本未定，或作《閨範圖說》跋，名曰《憂危竑議》，大指言貴妃欲奪儲位，坤陰助之，並及張養蒙、魏允貞等九人，語極妄誕。

translations.literal: At that time the heir was not settled; someone wrote a postface to the work called The Mysterious Discussion of Peril, chiefly saying the consort wished to seize the heirship and that Kun secretly aided her, also implicating Zhang Yangmeng, Wei Yunzhen, and nine others—language utterly absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Before the heir was settled, someone forged a postface, The Mysterious Discussion of Peril, claiming the consort plotted with Kun to seize the succession.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，皇太子立。

translations.literal: More than three years passed and the crown prince was established.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the crown prince was named.

sentences.zh: 至三十一年十一月甲子昧爽，自朝房至勛戚大臣門，各有匿名書一帙，名曰《續憂危竑議》，言貴妃與大學士朱賡，戎政尚書王世揚，三邊總督李汶，保定巡撫孫瑋，少卿張養誌，錦衣都督王之楨，千戶王名世、王承恩等相結，謀易太子，其言益妄誕不經。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month of the thirty-first year, at dawn on the jiazi day, from the court chambers to the doors of meritorious ministers and great kin, each received an anonymous booklet called Continuation of the Mysterious Discussion of Peril, saying the consort had joined Chief Grand Secretary Zhu Geng, Minister of War Affairs Wang Shiyang, supreme commander of the three frontiers Li Wen, Baoding grand coordinator Sun Wei, Vice Minister Zhang Yangzhi, Brocade Guard commander Wang Zhizhen, centurions Wang Mingshi and Wang Chengen, and others to plot replacing the crown prince—still more absurd.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one anonymous booklets, Continuation of the Mysterious Discussion of Peril, accused the consort and ministers of plotting to replace the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 矩獲之以聞，大學士賡奏亦入。

translations.literal: Ju seized them and reported; Grand Secretary Geng's memorial also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported the booklets; Zhu Geng's memorial followed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，敕矩及錦衣衛大索，必得造妖書者。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered Ju and the Brocade Guard to search thoroughly and must find who made the seditious book.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ju and the Brocade Guard to find the author at all costs.

sentences.zh: 時大獄猝發，緝校交錯都下，以風影捕系，所株連甚眾。

translations.literal: The great case broke suddenly; investigators crisscrossed the capital and seized people on suspicion; those implicated were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators crisscrossed the capital and implicated many on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 之楨欲陷錦衣指揮周嘉慶，首輔沈一貫欲陷次輔沈鯉、侍郎郭正域，俱使人屬矩。

translations.literal: Zhizhen wished to frame Brocade Guard commander Zhou Jiaqing; chief grand secretary Shen Yiguan wished to frame second grand secretary Shen Li and Vice Minister Guo Zhengyu—all sent men to ask Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhen tried to frame Zhou Jiaqing; Shen Yiguan tried to frame Shen Li and Guo Zhengyu—all asked Ju to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 矩正色拒之。

translations.literal: Ju sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ju refused.

sentences.zh: 已而百戶蔣臣捕生光至。

translations.literal: Later centurion Jiang Chen arrested Sheng Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion Jiang Chen arrested Sheng Guang.

sentences.zh: 生光者，京師無賴人也，嘗偽作富商包繼誌詩，有「鄭主乘黃屋」之句，以脅國泰及繼誌金，故人疑而捕之。

translations.literal: Sheng Guang was a Beijing ruffian who had once forged a wealthy merchant Bao Jizhi's poem with the line "Lord Zheng rides the yellow house" to extort gold from Guotai and Jizhi; people therefore suspected and arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Guang was a ruffian who had forged a poem extorting Guotai and Jizhi—people suspected him and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 酷訊不承，妻妾子弟皆掠治無完膚。

translations.literal: Under cruel interrogation he would not confess; wife, concubines, sons, and younger brothers were all tortured until not an unbruised patch remained.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he would not confess; his whole family was beaten raw.

sentences.zh: 矩心念生光即冤，然前罪已當死，且獄無主名，上必怒甚，恐輾轉攀累無已。

translations.literal: Ju thought that even if Sheng Guang were wronged, his earlier crime already warranted death, and with no named culprit the emperor would be very angry and fear endless implication.
translations.idiomatic: Ju knew Sheng Guang was likely innocent but feared endless implication if no culprit were named.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李廷機亦以生光前詩與妖書詞合。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Tingji also said Sheng Guang's earlier poem matched the seditious book's wording.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingji said Sheng Guang's earlier poem matched the booklet.

sentences.zh: 乃具獄，生光坐淩遲死。

translations.literal: The case was then closed; Sheng Guang was sentenced to death by slicing.
translations.idiomatic: The case closed with Sheng Guang executed by slicing.

sentences.zh: 鯉、正域、嘉慶及株連者，皆賴矩得全。

translations.literal: Shen Li, Guo Zhengyu, Jiaqing, and those implicated were all saved thanks to Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li, Guo Zhengyu, Jiaqing, and others were saved by Ju.

sentences.zh: 三十三年掌司禮監，督廠如故。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial while still supervising the depot as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-three he headed the Directorate of Ceremonial while keeping the depot.

sentences.zh: 帝欲杖建言參政姜士昌，以矩諫而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to beat remonstrating Administrator Jiang Shichang; Ju remonstrated and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to beat Jiang Shichang; Ju stopped it.

sentences.zh: 雲南民殺稅監楊榮，帝欲盡捕亂者，亦以矩言獲免。

translations.literal: When Yunnan people killed tax supervisor Yang Rong, the emperor wished to arrest all rioters; they were also spared on Ju's word.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan killed Yang Rong, the emperor wanted mass arrests; Ju spared them.

sentences.zh: 明年奉詔慮囚，御史曹學程以阻封日本酋關白事，系獄且十年，法司請於矩求出，矩謝不敢。

translations.literal: The next year he received an edict to review prisoners; censor Cao Xuecheng, for obstructing enfeoffment of Japan's ruler Hideyoshi, had been in prison nearly ten years; the law courts asked Ju to release him and Ju declined.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, reviewing prisoners, Ju declined to release Cao Xuecheng, jailed ten years for opposing Hideyoshi's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 已而密白之，竟重釋，余亦多所平反。

translations.literal: Later he secretly told the emperor and Cao was heavily released after all; many others were also reversed.
translations.idiomatic: He later secretly secured Cao's release and reversed many sentences.

sentences.zh: 又明年卒，賜祠額曰清忠。

translations.literal: The year after he died and was granted the shrine title Clear Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and received the shrine title Clear Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自馮保、張誠、張鯉相繼獲罪，其黨有所懲，不敢大肆。

translations.literal: From Feng Bao, Zhang Cheng, and Zhang Jing being punished in succession, their factions were somewhat restrained and did not run wild.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Bao, Zhang Cheng, and Zhang Jing fell, their factions were restrained.

sentences.zh: 帝亦惡其黨盛，有缺多不補。

translations.literal: The emperor also hated their faction's strength and often left vacancies unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also left many eunuch posts vacant.

sentences.zh: 迨晚年，用事者寥寥，東廠獄中至生青草。

translations.literal: By his later years those in power were few; in the Eastern Depot prison grass even grew.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years few eunuchs held power; grass grew in the Eastern Depot prison.

sentences.zh: 帝常膳舊以司禮輪供，後司禮無人，乾清宮管事牌子常雲獨辦，以故偵卒稀簡，中外相安。

translations.literal: The emperor's regular meals had been supplied in rotation by the Directorate of Ceremonial; later with no Ceremonial staff, Qianqing Palace steward Chang Yun alone managed it, so spies were few and inner and outer were relatively at peace.
translations.idiomatic: With Ceremonial posts empty, steward Chang Yun alone fed the emperor and spies grew rare.

sentences.zh: 惟四方采榷者，帝實縱之，故貪殘肆虐，民心憤怨，尋致禍亂雲。

translations.literal: Only the tax collectors in every region the emperor truly indulged; therefore they were greedy and cruel and popular resentment led to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Only mining-tax eunuchs he indulged remained greedy and cruel until rebellion followed.

sentences.zh: 初，西宮李選侍怙寵陵熹宗生母王才人，安內忿不平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Western Palace Lady Li, relying on favor, bullied Xizong's birth mother Lady Wang; Wang An inwardly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of the Western Palace bullied Lady Wang, Xizong's mother; Wang An resented it.

sentences.zh: 及光宗崩，選侍與心腹閹李進忠等謀挾皇長子自重，安發其謀於漣。

translations.literal: When Guangzong died, Lady Li and her trusted eunuch Li Jinzhong and others plotted to hold the eldest imperial son hostage to magnify themselves; An revealed the plot to Yang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong died, Lady Li and eunuch Li Jinzhong plotted to hold the heir hostage; An told Yang Lian.

sentences.zh: 漣偕一燝等入臨，安紿選侍抱皇長子出，擇吉即位，選侍移別宮去。

translations.literal: Lian with Wei Yifan and others entered to attend the death; An tricked Lady Li into bringing out the eldest son, chose an auspicious day for enthronement, and Lady Li moved to another palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lian and Yifan attended the deathbed; An brought out the heir and Lady Li was moved aside.

sentences.zh: 事詳一燝等傳。

translations.literal: The matter is detailed in the biographies of Yifan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is told in Yifan's biography.

sentences.zh: 熹宗心德安，言無不納。

translations.literal: Xizong was grateful to An in his heart and accepted his every word.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong trusted An completely.

sentences.zh: 安為人剛直而疏，又善病，不能數見帝。

translations.literal: An was upright but blunt by nature and often ill, and could not see the emperor often.
translations.idiomatic: An was blunt and often ill, so he seldom saw the emperor.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢始進，自結於安名下魏朝，朝日夕譽忠賢，安信之。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian first advanced he attached himself to An's follower Wei Chao; Chao praised Zhongxian day and night and An trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian attached to An's man Wei Chao, who praised him until An trusted him.

sentences.zh: 及安怒朝與忠賢爭客氏也，勒朝退，而忠賢、客氏日得志，忌安甚。

translations.literal: When An grew angry that Chao and Zhongxian quarreled over Lady Ke, he forced Chao to retire while Zhongxian and Ke daily gained their will and hated An deeply.
translations.idiomatic: An ousted Chao over Lady Ke while Zhongxian and Ke grew powerful and hated An.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年五月，帝命安掌司禮監，安以故事辭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tianqi the emperor ordered An to take charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial; An declined on precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianqi 1 the emperor ordered An to head Ceremonial; An declined on precedent.

sentences.zh: 客氏勸帝從其請，與忠賢謀殺之。

translations.literal: Lady Ke urged the emperor to accept his request and plotted with Zhongxian to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke urged acceptance of his resignation and plotted his murder with Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢猶豫未忍，客氏曰：「爾我孰若西李，而欲遺患耶？」

translations.literal: Zhongxian hesitated and could not bear it; Lady Ke said: "Are you and I not like Western Li? Why leave a future trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian hesitated; Lady Ke said, "Are we not like Western Li—why leave a future enemy?

sentences.zh: 忠賢意乃決，嗾給事中霍維華論安，降充南海子凈軍，而以劉朝為南海子提督，使殺安。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's mind was then decided; he incited supervising secretary Huo Weihua to impeach An, demoted him to purifying soldier at the Southern Park, and made Liu Chao director there to kill An.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian incited Huo Weihua to impeach An, demoted him to the Southern Park, and sent Liu Chao to kill him.

sentences.zh: 劉朝者，李選侍私閹，故以移宮盜庫下獄宥出者。

translations.literal: Liu Chao was Lady Li's private eunuch, released from prison after the palace-shift theft case.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao was Lady Li's eunuch, freed after the palace-shift theft case.

sentences.zh: 既至，絕安食。

translations.literal: Once there he cut off An's food.
translations.idiomatic: He cut off An's food.

sentences.zh: 安取籬落中蘆菔啖之，三日猶不死，乃撲殺之。

translations.literal: An took radishes from the fence to eat; after three days he still did not die and was then beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: An ate fence radishes; after three days Liu beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 安死三年，忠賢遂誣東林諸人與安交通，興大獄，清流之禍烈矣。

translations.literal: Three years after An's death Zhongxian falsely charged Eastern Lodge men with communicating with An and raised a great case; the calamity of the clear stream was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Zhongxian framed Eastern Lodge men as An's allies and unleashed the great purge.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝立，賜祠額曰昭忠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne he granted the shrine title Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chongzhen granted him the shrine title Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢，肅寧人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian was a man of Suning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was from Suning.

sentences.zh: 少無賴，與群惡少博，少勝，為所苦，恚而自宮，變姓名曰李進忠。

translations.literal: In youth he was a good-for-nothing; he gambled with wicked youths and when he lost was tormented by them; in rage he castrated himself and changed his name to Li Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he gambled, lost, castrated himself in rage, and took the name Li Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 其後乃復姓，賜名忠賢雲。

translations.literal: Later he resumed his surname and was given the name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resumed Wei and received the name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢自萬曆中選入宮，隸太監孫暹，夤緣入甲字庫，又求為皇長孫母王才人典膳，諂事魏朝。

translations.literal: Zhongxian entered the palace in the Wanli reign, served under eunuch Sun Xian, curried favor into the A-character storehouse, then sought to be steward of meals for the eldest imperial grandson's mother Lady Wang, and fawned on Wei Chao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered palace service under Sun Xian, reached the A-storehouse, became Lady Wang's meal steward, and fawned on Wei Chao.

sentences.zh: 朝數稱忠賢於安，安亦善遇之。

translations.literal: Chao often praised Zhongxian to An and An also treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Chao praised him to Wang An, who favored him.

sentences.zh: 長孫乳媼曰客氏，素私侍朝，所謂對食者也。

translations.literal: The eldest grandson's wet nurse was called Lady Ke; she had long privately served Chao—the so-called paired eating.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's wet nurse Lady Ke had long been Chao's "paired eating" partner.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢入，又通焉。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian entered he also had relations with her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian also took up with her.

sentences.zh: 客氏遂薄朝而愛忠賢，兩人深相結。

translations.literal: Lady Ke then slighted Chao and loved Zhongxian; the two were deeply joined.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke turned from Chao to Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 光宗崩，長孫嗣立，是為熹宗。

translations.literal: When Guangzong died the eldest grandson succeeded—this was Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong died the grandson succeeded as Xizong.

sentences.zh: 忠賢、客氏並有寵。

translations.literal: Zhongxian and Lady Ke both had favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian and Lady Ke both won favor.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，封客氏奉聖夫人，蔭其子侯國興、弟客光先及忠賢兄釗俱錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: Within a month Lady Ke was enfeoffed as Lady of Sagely Devotion; her son Hou Guoxing, younger brother Ke Guangxian, and Zhongxian's elder brother Zhao were all given Brocade Guard posts as commanders of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Lady Ke was ennobled; her kin and Zhongxian's brother won Brocade Guard posts.

sentences.zh: 忠賢尋自惜薪司遷司禮秉筆太監兼提督寶和三店。

translations.literal: Zhongxian soon moved from the Fuelwood Office to Ceremonial director and also supervised the Treasure, Harmony, and Three Shops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian rose from Fuelwood to Ceremonial director and supervised palace shops.

sentences.zh: 忠賢不識字，例不當入司禮，以客氏故，得之。

translations.literal: Zhongxian could not read and by rule should not enter Ceremonial; because of Lady Ke he obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate, he should not have entered Ceremonial—but Lady Ke secured it.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年詔賜客氏香火田，敘忠賢治皇祖陵功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi an edict granted Lady Ke incense-field lands and credited Zhongxian with merit in tending the imperial ancestor tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 1 granted Lady Ke temple lands and credited Zhongxian with tomb merit.

sentences.zh: 御史王心一諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Xinyi remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Xinyi objected in vain.

sentences.zh: 及帝大婚，御史畢佐周、劉蘭請遣客氏出外，大學士劉一燝亦言之。

translations.literal: When the emperor's grand wedding came, censors Bi Zuozhou and Liu Lan asked that Lady Ke be sent out; Chief Grand Secretary Liu Yifan also spoke.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand wedding, censors and Liu Yifan asked to send Lady Ke out.

sentences.zh: 帝戀戀不忍舍，曰：「皇后幼，賴媼保護，俟皇祖大葬議之。」

translations.literal: The emperor lingered and could not bear to let her go, saying: "The empress is young and relies on the nurse for protection; after the imperial ancestor's great burial We shall discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused: "The empress is young and needs her nurse until the imperial burial.

sentences.zh: 忠賢顓客氏，逐魏朝。

translations.literal: Zhongxian monopolized Lady Ke and drove off Wei Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian monopolized Lady Ke and drove off Wei Chao.

sentences.zh: 又忌王安持正，謀殺之，盡斥安名下諸閹。

translations.literal: He also hated Wang An's uprightness, plotted to kill him, and expelled all eunuchs under An's name.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted against upright Wang An, killed him, and expelled his followers.

sentences.zh: 客氏淫而狠。

translations.literal: Lady Ke was licentious and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke was licentious and cruel.

sentences.zh: 忠賢不知書，頗強記，猜忍陰毒，好諛。

translations.literal: Zhongxian could not read but had a strong memory; he was suspicious, cruel, and secretive and loved flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was illiterate but cunning, cruel, and addicted to flattery.

sentences.zh: 帝深信任此兩人，兩人勢益張，用司禮臨王體乾及李永貞、石元雅、塗文輔等為羽翼，宮中人莫敢忤。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply trusted these two; their power grew; he used Ceremonial overseer Wang Tigan and Li Yongzhen, Shi Yuanya, Tu Wenfu, and others as wings; no one in the palace dared oppose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted them utterly; Wang Tigan, Li Yongzhen, and others became their wings.

sentences.zh: 既而客氏出，復召入。

translations.literal: Later Lady Ke went out and was recalled again.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke was sent out, then recalled.

sentences.zh: 御史周宗建、侍郎陳邦瞻、御史馬鳴起、給事中侯震昜先後力諍，俱被詰責。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Zongjian, Vice Minister Chen Bangzhan, censor Ma Mingqi, and supervising secretary Hou Zhenyi remonstrated forcefully in succession; all were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zongjian, Chen Bangzhan, Ma Mingqi, and Hou Zhenyi remonstrated and were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 給事中倪思輝、朱欽相、王心一復言之，並謫外，尚未指及忠賢也。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang, and Wang Xinyi spoke again and were all demoted outside the capital, not yet naming Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang, and Wang Xinyi spoke again and were banished—still without naming Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢乃勸帝選武閹、煉火器為內操，密結大學士沈纮為援。

translations.literal: Zhongxian then urged the emperor to choose martial eunuchs and train fire weapons as inner guards and secretly joined Chief Grand Secretary Shen Que as support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian trained martial eunuchs as inner guards and enlisted Shen Que.

sentences.zh: 又日引帝為倡優聲伎，狗馬射獵。

translations.literal: He also daily led the emperor to actors, music, dogs, horses, and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He led the emperor to actors, music, hunting, and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事劉宗周首劾之，帝大怒，賴大學士葉向高救免。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice director Liu Zongzhou first impeached him; the emperor was greatly angered and Liu was spared only thanks to Chief Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou first impeached him; the emperor raged but Ye Xianggao saved him.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗在位久，怠於政事，章奏多不省。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shenzong had long been on the throne and was slack in government affairs; memorials were often not reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Shenzong had neglected government and ignored memorials.

sentences.zh: 廷臣漸立門戶，以危言激論相尚，國本之爭，指斥宮禁。

translations.literal: Court officials gradually formed partisan camps, vying in alarming rhetoric and inflammatory speech; disputes over the succession pointed blame at the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials formed rival factions, competing in shrill rhetoric; succession struggles turned their fire on the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宰輔大臣為言者所彈擊，輒引疾避去。

translations.literal: Chief ministers attacked by remonstrators would at once plead illness and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrators attacked them, chief ministers would plead illness and quit.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎顧憲成講學東林書院，海內士大夫多附之，「東林」之名自是始。

translations.literal: Department of Personnel section chief Gu Xiancheng lectured at the Donglin Academy; scholars throughout the realm flocked to him, and the name "Donglin" dates from this.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiancheng of the Personnel Department taught at the Donglin Academy; scholars nationwide rallied to him, and the name "Donglin" began here.

sentences.zh: 既而「梃擊」、「紅丸」、「移宮」三案起，盈廷如聚訟。

translations.literal: Then the three cases—the Stick Beating, the Red Pill, and the Palace Shift—arose, and the whole court wrangled like litigants.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the Stick Beating, Red Pill, and Palace Shift cases, and the court erupted in factional quarrels.

sentences.zh: 與東林忤者，眾目之為邪黨。

translations.literal: Those who crossed the Donglin were widely seen as a wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who opposed the Donglin was branded a wicked faction.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，廢斥殆盡，識者已憂其過激變生。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianqi they were nearly all purged; perceptive men already feared their excess would breed disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi the purge was nearly complete; wise observers already feared the backlash.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢勢成，其黨果謀倚之以傾東林。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian's power was secure, his faction indeed plotted to lean on him to overturn the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongxian was entrenched, his followers plotted to use him to destroy the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 而徐大化、霍維華、孫傑首附忠賢，劉一燝及尚書周嘉謨並為傑劾去。

translations.literal: Xu Dahua, Huo Weihua, and Sun Jie were first to attach to Zhongxian; Liu Yihuan and Minister Zhou Jiamo were both impeached out of office by Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dahua, Huo Weihua, and Sun Jie were first to join Zhongxian; Sun Jie impeached Liu Yihuan and Minister Zhou Jiamo from office.

sentences.zh: 然是時葉向高、韓爌方輔政，鄒元標、趙南星、王紀、高攀龍等皆居大僚，左光斗、魏大中、黃尊素等在言路，皆力持清議，忠賢未克逞。

translations.literal: Yet at this time Ye Xianggao and Han Kuang were assisting government; Zou Yuanbiao, Zhao Nanxing, Wang Ji, Gao Panlong, and others held high posts; Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Huang Zunsu, and others held remonstrating posts—all forcefully upheld pure opinion, and Zhongxian could not yet have his way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ye Xianggao and Han Kuang governed; Zou Yuanbiao, Zhao Nanxing, Wang Ji, and Gao Panlong held high office; Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and Huang Zunsu held remonstrating posts—they upheld righteous opinion, and Zhongxian could not yet prevail.

sentences.zh: 二年敘慶陵功，蔭忠賢弟侄錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the second year, for merit at Qingling, Zhongxian's younger brother and nephew were granted hereditary posts as assistant commanders in the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, for Qingling merit, Zhongxian's brother and nephew won Brocade Guard assistant command posts.

sentences.zh: 給事中惠世揚、尚書王紀論沈纮交通客、魏，俱被譴去。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Hui Shiyang and Minister Wang Ji denounced Shen Hong for colluding with Lady Ke and Wei Zhongxian; both were rebuked and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shiyang and Wang Ji denounced Shen Hong for colluding with Lady Ke and Zhongxian; both were punished and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會初夏雨雹，周宗建言雹不以時，忠賢讒慝所致。

translations.literal: When hail fell in early summer, Zhou Zongjian said the hail came out of season and was caused by Zhongxian's slander and malice.
translations.idiomatic: Early-summer hail prompted Zhou Zongjian to blame Zhongxian's slander and malice.

sentences.zh: 修撰文震孟、太僕少卿滿朝薦相繼言之，亦俱黜。

translations.literal: Drafting secretary Wen Zhenmeng and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Manchao Jian spoke in succession; they too were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting secretary Wen Zhenmeng and Vice Minister Manchao Jian spoke next; they too were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三年春，引其私人魏廣微為大學士。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he brought in his private man Wei Guangwei as grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year three he installed his man Wei Guangwei as grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 令御史郭鞏訐宗建、一燝、元標及楊漣、周朝瑞等保舉熊廷弼，黨邪誤國。

translations.literal: He had censor Guo Gong accuse Zongjian, Yihuan, Yuanbiao, Yang Lian, Zhou Chaorui, and others of recommending Xiong Tingbi and thus abetting wicked factions to harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: He had censor Guo Gong accuse Zongjian, Yihuan, Yuanbiao, Yang Lian, and Zhou Chaorui of backing Xiong Tingbi and abetting factional evil.

sentences.zh: 宗建駁鞏受忠賢指揮，御史方大任助宗建攻鞏及忠賢，皆不勝。

translations.literal: Zongjian rebutted that Gong acted on Zhongxian's orders; censor Fang Daren helped Zongjian attack Gong and Zhongxian—but all failed.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian rebutted that Gong obeyed Zhongxian; Fang Daren joined the attack—but they lost.

sentences.zh: 其秋，詔忠賢及客氏子國興所蔭錦衣官並世襲。

translations.literal: That autumn an edict granted hereditary Brocade Guard posts to Zhongxian and to Guo Xing, son of Lady Ke, through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an edict made Zhongxian's and Lady Ke's son Guo Xing's Brocade Guard posts hereditary.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書董漢儒、給事中程註、御史汪泗論交諫，不從。

translations.literal: Minister of War Dong Hanru, supervising secretary Cheng Zhu, and censor Wang Si remonstrated together; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dong Hanru, Cheng Zhu, and censor Wang Si remonstrated together in vain.

sentences.zh: 忠賢益無忌，增置內操萬人，衷甲出入，恣為威虐。

translations.literal: Zhongxian grew utterly unrestrained: he added ten thousand inner guards, went about armored, and indulged in terror and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian grew brazen—ten thousand inner guards, armor in the palace, terror and cruelty unchecked.

sentences.zh: 矯詔賜光宗選侍趙氏死。

translations.literal: By forged edict he had Guangzong's attendant Lady Zhao put to death.
translations.idiomatic: By forged edict he had Guangzong's attendant Lady Zhao executed.

sentences.zh: 裕妃張氏有娠，客氏譖殺之。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang of Yu was pregnant; Lady Ke slandered her and had her killed.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang of Yu was pregnant; Lady Ke slandered her to death.

sentences.zh: 又革成妃李氏封。

translations.literal: He also stripped Consort Li of Cheng of her title.
translations.idiomatic: He also stripped Consort Li of Cheng of her rank.

sentences.zh: 皇后張氏娠，客氏以計墮其胎，帝由此乏嗣。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang was pregnant; Lady Ke by a stratagem caused her to miscarry, and from this the emperor lacked heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang was pregnant; Lady Ke engineered a miscarriage, and the emperor thereafter had no heirs.

sentences.zh: 他所害宮嬪馮貴人等，太監王國臣、劉克敬、馬鑒等甚眾。

translations.literal: Other palace women he harmed, such as Lady Feng the Noble, and eunuchs Wang Guochen, Liu Kejing, Ma Jian, and many more.
translations.idiomatic: Other victims included Lady Feng and eunuchs Wang Guochen, Liu Kejing, Ma Jian, and many more.

sentences.zh: 禁掖事秘，莫詳也。

translations.literal: Inner-palace affairs were secret; none can be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Palace secrets leave the full toll unknown.

sentences.zh: 是冬，兼掌東廠事。

translations.literal: That winter he also took charge of Eastern Depot affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he also took charge of the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 四年，給事中傅櫆結忠賢甥傅應星為兄弟，誣奏中書汪文言，並及左光斗、魏大中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, supervising secretary Fu Chu allied with Zhongxian's nephew Fu Yingxing as sworn brothers and falsely impeached Secretariat drafter Wang Wenyan, implicating Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, Fu Chu swore brotherhood with Zhongxian's nephew Fu Yingxing and falsely impeached Wang Wenyan, implicating Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 下文言鎮撫獄，將大行羅織。

translations.literal: Wang was sent to the prison of the Brocade Guard; a great frame-up was about to unfold.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was sent to the guard prison; a great frame-up was underway.

sentences.zh: 掌鎮撫劉僑受葉向高教，止坐文言。

translations.literal: Prison warden Liu Qiao, taught by Ye Xianggao, convicted only Wenyan.
translations.idiomatic: Warden Liu Qiao, coached by Ye Xianggao, convicted only Wenyan.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大怒，削僑籍，而以私人許顯純代。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was furious, stripped Qiao of rank, and replaced him with his man Xu Xianchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian raged, stripped Qiao of rank, and installed Xu Xianchun.

sentences.zh: 是時御史李應升以內操諫，給事中霍守曲以忠賢乞祠額諫，御史劉廷佐以忠賢濫蔭諫，給事中沈惟炳以立枷諫，忠賢皆矯旨詰責。

translations.literal: At this time censor Li Yingsheng remonstrated over inner guards; supervising secretary Huo Shouqu over Zhongxian's plea for a temple plaque; censor Liu Tingzuo over Zhongxian's lavish hereditary grants; supervising secretary Shen Weibing over the standing cangue—all were rebuked by forged edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Yingsheng, Huo Shouqu, Liu Tingzuo, and Shen Weibing remonstrated on inner guards, temple plaques, lavish grants, and the cangue—Zhongxian answered each with forged rebukes.

sentences.zh: 於是副都御史楊漣憤甚，劾忠賢二十四大罪。

translations.literal: Then Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Lian, enraged, impeached Zhongxian on twenty-four major crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Then Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian for twenty-four major crimes.

sentences.zh: 疏上，忠賢懼，求解於韓爌不應，遂趨帝前泣訴，且辭東廠，而客氏從旁為剖析，體乾等翼之。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne Zhongxian was afraid; he begged Han Kuang for help and got no answer, then rushed before the emperor weeping, even offering to quit the Eastern Depot—while Lady Ke parsed matters at his side and Tigan and others backed him.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial terrified Zhongxian; Han Kuang refused help; he wept before the emperor and offered to quit the Depot while Lady Ke and Tigan defended him.

sentences.zh: 帝懵然不辨也。

translations.literal: The emperor was dazed and could not tell truth from falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was too confused to judge.

sentences.zh: 遂溫諭留忠賢，而於次日下漣疏，嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: He then gently ordered Zhongxian to stay, and the next day issued Lian's memorial with a stern rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: He gently kept Zhongxian—and the next day rebuked Lian harshly.

sentences.zh: 漣既絀，魏大中及給事中陳良訓、許譽卿，撫寧侯朱國弼，南京兵部尚書陳道亨，侍郎嶽元聲等七十餘人，交章論忠賢不法。

translations.literal: Once Lian was disgraced, Wei Dazhong and supervising secretaries Chen Liangxun and Xu Yuqing, Marquis Zhu Guobi, Nanjing Minister of War Chen Daohang, Vice Minister Yue Yuansheng, and more than seventy others submitted memorial after memorial denouncing Zhongxian's lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: After Lian's disgrace, Wei Dazhong, Chen Liangxun, Xu Yuqing, Zhu Guobi, Chen Daohang, Yue Yuansheng, and seventy others denounced Zhongxian's lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 向高及禮部尚書翁正春請遣忠賢歸私第以塞謗，不許。

translations.literal: Xianggao and Minister of Rites Weng Zhengchun asked that Zhongxian be sent to his private residence to silence slander; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao and Weng Zhengchun asked to send Zhongxian home to silence slander; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢憤甚，欲盡殺異己者。

translations.literal: At this time Zhongxian was furious and wished to kill every dissenting man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian now wanted every opponent dead.

sentences.zh: 顧秉謙因陰籍其所忌姓名授忠賢，使以次斥逐。

translations.literal: Gu Bingqian secretly copied the names of those he resented and gave the list to Zhongxian, who drove them out one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian secretly listed his enemies for Zhongxian, who expelled them one by one.

sentences.zh: 王體乾復昌言用廷杖，威脅廷臣。

translations.literal: Wang Tigan again loudly advocated court beatings to intimidate the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tigan again urged court beatings to terrorize officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，工部郎中萬燝上疏刺忠賢，立杖死。

translations.literal: Before long, Bureau of Works section chief Wan Huang memorialized attacking Zhongxian and was beaten to death on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bureau of Works chief Wan Huang attacked Zhongxian in a memorial and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 又以御史林汝翥事辱向高，向高遂致仕去，汝翥亦予杖。

translations.literal: Also over censor Lin Ruzhu's affair he shamed Xianggao; Xianggao then retired, and Ruzhu was beaten too.
translations.idiomatic: Over censor Lin Ruzhu he humiliated Xianggao into retirement; Ruzhu was beaten as well.

sentences.zh: 廷臣俱大詟。

translations.literal: Court officials were all deeply terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The court was terrified.

sentences.zh: 一時罷斥者，吏部尚書趙南星、左都御史高攀龍、吏部侍郎陳於廷及楊漣、左光斗、魏大中等先後數十人，已又逐韓爌及兵部侍郎李邦華。

translations.literal: In one sweep were dismissed Minister Zhao Nanxing, Censor-in-Chief Gao Panlong, Vice Minister Chen Yuting, and Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and dozens more in succession; then Han Kuang and Vice Minister of War Li Banghua were also driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Chen Yuting, Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and dozens more fell in succession; then Han Kuang and Li Banghua followed.

sentences.zh: 正人去國，紛紛若振槁。

translations.literal: Righteous men left the state; they fell like dry stalks in a wind.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous men fled the court like dry stalks in a gale.

sentences.zh: 乃矯中旨召用例轉科道。

translations.literal: Then by forged middle edict he summoned and appointed men transferred from precedent into the censorate and remonstrance bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: By forged edict he filled the censorate and remonstrance posts with his own transfers.

sentences.zh: 以朱童蒙、郭允厚為太僕少卿，呂鵬雲、孫傑為大理丞，復霍維華、郭興治為給事中，徐景濂、賈繼春、楊維垣為御史，而起徐兆魁、王紹徽、喬應甲、徐紹吉、阮大鋮、陳爾翌、張養素、李應薦、李嵩、楊春懋等，為之爪牙。

translations.literal: Zhu Tongmeng and Guo Yunhou were made vice ministers of the Imperial Stud; Lü Pengyun and Sun Jie vice directors of the Court of Judicial Review; Huo Weihua and Guo Xingzhi restored as supervising secretaries; Xu Jinglian, Jia Jichun, and Yang Weiyuan made censors; and Xu Zhaokui, Wang Shaohui, Qiao Yingjia, Xu Shaoji, Ruan Dacheng, Chen Eryi, Zhang Yangsu, Li Yingjian, Li Song, Yang Chunmao, and others were raised up as his claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Tongmeng, Yunhou, Pengyun, Sun Jie, Huo Weihua, Guo Xingzhi, Xu Jinglian, Jia Jichun, Yang Weiyuan, Xu Zhaokui, Wang Shaohui, Qiao Yingjia, and a host of others as his henchmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復用擬戍崔呈秀為御史。

translations.literal: Before long he restored Cui Chengxiu, who had been sentenced to frontier service, as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he restored Cui Chengxiu, slated for frontier exile, as censor.

sentences.zh: 呈秀乃造《天鑒》、《同志》諸錄，王紹徽亦造《點將錄》，皆以鄒元標、顧憲成、葉向高、劉一燝等為魁，盡羅入不附忠賢者，號曰東林黨人，獻於忠賢。

translations.literal: Chengxiu then compiled the Records of Heavenly Mirror and Records of Like Minds; Wang Shaohui also compiled the Record of Marshaling Generals—all naming Zou Yuanbiao, Gu Xiancheng, Ye Xianggao, Liu Yihuan, and others as ringleaders, sweeping in every man who would not follow Zhongxian, calling them Donglin partisans, and presenting the lists to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu compiled the Heavenly Mirror and Like Minds records; Wang Shaohui compiled the Record of Marshaling Generals—branding Zou Yuanbiao, Gu Xiancheng, Ye Xianggao, and Liu Yihuan as ringleaders and listing every opponent as a Donglin partisan.

sentences.zh: 忠賢喜，於是群小益求媚忠賢，攘臂攻東林矣。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was pleased; then the petty men strove all the more to flatter him and fell upon the Donglin with bare arms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted; his petty followers flattered him ever harder and fell upon the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 初，朝臣爭三案及辛亥、癸亥兩京察與熊廷弼獄事，忠賢本無預。

translations.literal: At first, when court officials quarreled over the three cases, the xinhai and guihai metropolitan reviews in the two capitals, and the Xiong Tingbi affair, Zhongxian had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhongxian had nothing to do with quarrels over the three cases, the xinhai and guihai reviews, or the Xiong Tingbi affair.

sentences.zh: 其黨欲藉忠賢力傾諸正人，遂相率歸忠賢，稱義兒，且云：「東林將害翁。」

translations.literal: His faction wished to borrow Zhongxian's strength to overturn upright men; they therefore flocked to him in succession, calling him sworn father, and saying: "The Donglin will harm the Old Man."
translations.idiomatic: His faction wanted his power to crush upright men; they flocked to him as sworn sons, saying, "The Donglin will harm the Old Man.

sentences.zh: 以故，忠賢欲甘心焉。

translations.literal: For this reason Zhongxian wished to destroy them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: So Zhongxian resolved to destroy them utterly.

sentences.zh: 御史張訥、倪文煥，給事中李魯生，工部主事曹欽程等，競搏擊善類為報復。

translations.literal: Censors Zhang Na and Ni Wenhuan, supervising secretary Li Lusheng, Bureau of Works section chief Cao Qincheng, and others vied to strike down good men in revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhang Na and Ni Wenhuan, Li Lusheng, Cao Qincheng, and others vied to destroy good men in revenge.

sentences.zh: 而御史梁夢環復興汪文言獄，下鎮撫司拷死。

translations.literal: Censor Liang Menghuan revived the Wang Wenyan case; Wang was sent to the guard prison and tortured to death.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liang Menghuan revived Wang Wenyan's case; he was tortured to death in the guard prison.

sentences.zh: 許顯純具爰書，詞連趙南星、楊漣等二十餘人，削籍遣戍有差。

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun drew up the indictment; the charges implicated Zhao Nanxing, Yang Lian, and more than twenty others, who were stripped of rank and sent to frontier service in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun's indictment implicated Zhao Nanxing, Yang Lian, and twenty others; ranks were stripped and exile assigned.

sentences.zh: 逮漣及左光斗、魏大中、周朝瑞、袁化中、顧大章等六人，至牽入熊廷弼案中，掠治死於獄。

translations.literal: Lian and Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Zhou Chaorui, Yuan Huazhong, and Gu Dazhang—six men in all—were arrested and dragged into the Xiong Tingbi case; under torture they died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Zhou Chaorui, Yuan Huazhong, and Gu Dazhang were arrested, tied to the Xiong Tingbi case, and tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 又殺廷弼，而杖其姻御史吳裕中至死。

translations.literal: Tingbi was also killed, and his in-law censor Wu Yuzhong was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbi was killed too, and his in-law Wu Yuzhong was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 又削逐尚書李宗延、張問達，侍郎公鼐等五十餘人，朝署一空。

translations.literal: Ministers Li Zongyan and Zhang Wenda, Vice Minister Gong Dai, and more than fifty others were also stripped and driven out; the court offices stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Li Zongyan and Zhang Wenda, Vice Minister Gong Dai, and fifty others were purged; the court was hollow.

sentences.zh: 而特召元詩教、劉述祖等為御史，私人悉不次超擢。

translations.literal: Special summons then made Yuan Shijiao and Liu Shuzu censors; private men were all promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shijiao and Liu Shuzu were specially summoned as censors; favorites were promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 於是忠賢之黨遍要津矣。

translations.literal: Thus Zhongxian's faction held every vital post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian's faction now held every vital post.

sentences.zh: 當是時，東廠番役橫行，所緝訪無論虛實輒糜爛。

translations.literal: At this time Eastern Depot runners ran rampant; whatever they investigated, true or false, ended in mangled corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot runners ran rampant; every investigation, true or false, ended in mangled corpses.

sentences.zh: 戚臣李承恩者，寧安大長公主子也，家藏公主賜器。

translations.literal: A kinsman by marriage, Li Chengen, was son of the Grand Princess of Ning'an; his household kept vessels the princess had bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengen, son of the Grand Princess of Ning'an, kept vessels the princess had bestowed.

sentences.zh: 忠賢誣以盜乘輿服御物，論死。

translations.literal: Zhongxian falsely charged him with stealing imperial carriage robes and regalia and sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian charged him with stealing imperial regalia and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 中書吳懷賢讀楊漣疏，擊節稱嘆。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Wu Huaixian read Yang Lian's memorial and beat his thigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Drafter Wu Huaixian read Yang Lian's memorial and beat his thigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 奴告之，斃懷賢，籍其家。

translations.literal: A slave reported him; Huaixian was beaten to death and his household confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: A slave reported him; Huaixian was beaten to death and his property seized.

sentences.zh: 武弁蔣應陽為廷弼訟冤，立誅死。

translations.literal: Military officer Jiang Yingyang pleaded Tingbi's innocence and was immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: Officer Jiang Yingyang pleaded Tingbi's innocence and was executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 民間偶語，或觸忠賢，輒被擒僇，甚至剝皮、刲舌，所殺不可勝數，道路以目。

translations.literal: Casual talk among the people that touched Zhongxian would bring capture and slaughter—even flaying and tongue-cutting; the dead were beyond counting, and people dared only glance in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Casual talk that touched Zhongxian brought capture, flaying, tongue-cutting, and death beyond counting; people dared only glance in the streets.

sentences.zh: 其年，敘門功，加恩三等，蔭都督同知。

translations.literal: That year, for merit at the gate, favor was increased by three grades and a hereditary post as vice commissioner was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for gate merit, favor rose three grades and a hereditary vice commissioner's post was granted.

sentences.zh: 又蔭其族叔魏志德都督僉事。

translations.literal: His clansman Wei Zhide was also granted a hereditary post as assistant commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Wei Zhide won a hereditary assistant commissioner's post.

sentences.zh: 擢傅應星為左都督，且旌其母。

translations.literal: Fu Yingxing was promoted to left commissioner, and his mother was honored.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yingxing was made left commissioner and his mother honored.

sentences.zh: 而以魏良卿僉書錦衣衛，掌南鎮撫司事。

translations.literal: Wei Liangqing was appointed to sign for the Brocade Guard and take charge of the southern guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangqing was put in charge of the Brocade Guard and the southern guard prison.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，鹵簿大駕成，蔭都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, when the imperial guard of honor was complete, a hereditary assistant commissioner's post was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year six, when the imperial guard of honor was complete, an assistant commissioner's post was granted.

sentences.zh: 復使其黨李永貞偽為浙江太監李實奏，逮治前應天巡撫周起元及江、浙裏居諸臣高攀龍、周宗建、繆昌期、周順昌、黃尊素、李應升等。

translations.literal: Again his follower Li Yongzhen forged a memorial in the name of Zhejiang eunuch Li Shi, arresting former Suzhou grand coordinator Zhou Qiyuan and retired officials in Jiangsu and Zhejiang—Gao Panlong, Zhou Zongjian, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang, Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Follower Li Yongzhen forged a memorial as Zhejiang eunuch Li Shi, arresting Zhou Qiyuan and retired Jiangsu-Zhejiang officials including Gao Panlong, Zhou Zongjian, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang, Huang Zunsu, and Li Yingsheng.

sentences.zh: 攀龍赴水死，順昌等六人死獄中。

translations.literal: Panlong drowned himself; Shunchang and five others died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong drowned; Shunchang and five others died in prison.

sentences.zh: 蘇州民見順昌逮，不平，毆殺二校尉，巡撫毛一鷺為捕顏佩韋等五人悉誅死。

translations.literal: When Suzhou people saw Shunchang arrested they rose in anger, beat two guard runners to death; Grand Coordinator Mao Yilu arrested Yan Peiwei and four others and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou rose when Shunchang was taken, killed two guard runners; Mao Yilu arrested Yan Peiwei and four others and executed them.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書徐兆魁治獄，視忠賢所怒，即坐大辟。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Xu Zhaokui tried cases: whomever Zhongxian hated he sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Zhaokui tried cases—whomever Zhongxian hated died.

sentences.zh: 又從霍維華言，命顧秉謙等修《三朝要典》，極意詆諸黨人惡。

translations.literal: Again following Huo Weihua's advice, he ordered Gu Bingqian and others to compile the Essentials of Three Reigns, vilifying the wickedness of the factional men with all their might.
translations.idiomatic: Following Huo Weihua, he ordered Gu Bingqian to compile the Essentials of Three Reigns, vilifying the faction with all their might.

sentences.zh: 御史徐復陽請毀講學書院，以絕黨根。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Fuyang asked to destroy the lecture academies and cut off the faction at the root.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Fuyang asked to destroy lecture academies and uproot the faction.

sentences.zh: 御史盧承欽又請立東林黨碑。

translations.literal: Censor Lu Chengqin also asked to erect a stele listing Donglin partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Chengqin asked for a stele listing Donglin partisans.

sentences.zh: 海內皆屏息喪氣。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm all held their breath and lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm people held their breath in despair.

sentences.zh: 霍維華遂教忠賢冒邊功矣。

translations.literal: Huo Weihua then taught Zhongxian to claim frontier merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Weihua then taught Zhongxian to claim false frontier merit.

sentences.zh: 遼陽男子武長春遊妓家，有妄言，東廠擒之。

translations.literal: A man of Liaoyang, Wu Changchun, visiting a brothel spoke reckless words; the Eastern Depot seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changchun of Liaoyang spoke recklessly in a brothel; the Eastern Depot seized him.

sentences.zh: 許顯純掠治，故張其辭云：「長春敵間，不獲且為亂，賴廠臣忠智立奇勛。」

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun tortured him and deliberately inflated his confession, saying: "Changchun was an enemy spy; had he not been caught he would have raised rebellion; thanks to the depot chief's loyalty and wisdom a great merit was achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun tortured him and inflated his confession: "Changchun was an enemy spy who would have rebelled; the depot chief's loyalty saved the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔封忠賢侄良卿為肅寧伯，賜宅第、莊田，頒鐵券。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Zhongxian's nephew Liangqing as Baron of Suning, granted mansions and estates, and issued an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Liangqing Baron of Suning, granted mansions, estates, and an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王紹徽請崇其先世，詔贈忠賢四代如本爵。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Shaohui asked to honor his ancestors; an edict posthumously ennobled four generations of Zhongxian's forebears at his own rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaohui asked to honor Zhongxian's ancestors; four generations were posthumously ennobled at his rank.

sentences.zh: 忠賢又矯詔遣其黨太監劉應坤、陶文、紀用鎮山海關，收攬兵柄。

translations.literal: Zhongxian again by forged edict sent his followers—the eunuchs Liu Yingkun, Tao Wen, and Ji Yong—to garrison Shanhai Pass and gather military power.
translations.idiomatic: By forged edict he sent Liu Yingkun, Tao Wen, and Ji Yong to garrison Shanhai Pass and seize military power.

sentences.zh: 再敘功，蔭都督同知，世襲錦衣衛指揮使，各一人。

translations.literal: Merit was again recorded; hereditary posts as vice commissioner and hereditary Brocade Guard commander were granted, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was recorded again; hereditary vice commissioner and Brocade Guard commander posts were granted.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫潘汝楨奏請為忠賢建祠。

translations.literal: Zhejiang grand coordinator Pan Ruzhen memorialized asking to build a shrine to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Ruzhen of Zhejiang asked to build a shrine to Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 倉場總督薛貞言草場火，以忠賢救，得無害。

translations.literal: Granary commissioner Xue Zhen said a hayfield fire was quenched by Zhongxian's rescue and no harm was done.
translations.idiomatic: Granary commissioner Xue Zhen claimed Zhongxian quenched a hayfield fire.

sentences.zh: 於是頌功德者相繼，諸祠皆自此始矣。

translations.literal: Then eulogies of merit followed one after another; shrines to him all began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogies followed; the cult of shrines to Zhongxian began here.

sentences.zh: 編修吳孔嘉與宗人吳養春有仇，誘養春仆告其主隱占黃山，養春父子瘐死。

translations.literal: Drafting secretary Wu Kongjia bore a grudge against his clansman Wu Yangchun; he induced Yangchun's slave to accuse his master of illegally occupying Mount Huang; father and son died in prison of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kongjia hated clansman Wu Yangchun; he induced a slave to accuse Yangchun of seizing Mount Huang; father and son died in prison.

sentences.zh: 忠賢遣主事呂下問、評事許誌吉先後往徽州籍其家，株蔓殘酷。

translations.literal: Zhongxian sent section chief Lü Xiawen and reviewer Xu Zhiji in succession to Huizhou to confiscate the household; the implicated suffered cruelly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian sent Lü Xiawen and Xu Zhiji to Huizhou to confiscate the estate; implicated kin suffered cruelly.

sentences.zh: 知府石萬程不忍，削髮去，徽州幾亂。

translations.literal: Prefect Shi Wancheng could not bear it, shaved his head, and left; Huizhou nearly erupted in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shi Wancheng shaved his head and fled; Huizhou nearly exploded.

sentences.zh: 其黨都督張體乾誣揚州知府劉鐸代李承恩謀釋獄，結道士方景陽詛忠賢，鐸竟斬。

translations.literal: His follower Commissioner Zhang Tigang falsely charged Yangzhou prefect Liu Duo with plotting on Li Chengen's behalf to free prisoners, joining the Daoist Fang Jingyang in cursing Zhongxian; Duo was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Follower Zhang Tigang charged Yangzhou prefect Liu Duo with plotting Li Chengen's release and joining Fang Jingyang in cursing Zhongxian; Duo was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又以睚眥怨，誣新城侯子錦衣王國興，論斬，並黜主事徐石麒。

translations.literal: Again over a petty grudge he falsely charged Marquis of Xincheng's son, Brocade Guard Wang Guoxing, sentenced him to death, and also dismissed section chief Xu Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Over a petty grudge he charged Marquis of Xincheng's son Wang Guoxing, had him beheaded, and dismissed Xu Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 御史門克新誣吳人顧同寅、孫文豸誄熊廷弼，坐妖言律斬。

translations.literal: Censor Men Kexin falsely charged Wu men Gu Tongyin and Sun Wenchi with composing a eulogy for Xiong Tingbi and sentenced them to death under the law on sorcerous speech.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Men Kexin charged Gu Tongyin and Sun Wenchi with eulogizing Xiong Tingbi and executed them under the sorcery law.

sentences.zh: 又逮侍郎王之寀，斃於獄。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Zhicai was also arrested and beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Zhicai was arrested and beaten to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 凡忠賢所宿恨，若韓爌、張問達、何士晉、程註等，雖已去，必削籍，重或充軍，死必追贓破其家。

translations.literal: All whom Zhongxian deeply hated—Han Kuang, Zhang Wenda, He Shijin, Cheng Zhu, and others—though already gone, were stripped of rank; the gravest were sent to military exile; if dead, their estates were pursued for restitution and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: All Zhongxian hated—Han Kuang, Zhang Wenda, He Shijin, Cheng Zhu—though gone, lost rank; the worst were exiled; the dead had their estates ruined for restitution.

sentences.zh: 或忠賢偶忘之，其黨必追論前事，激忠賢怒。

translations.literal: If Zhongxian happened to forget, his faction would surely revisit old grievances and stir his anger.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongxian forgot a grudge, his followers would revive it and stoke his rage.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，內外大權一歸忠賢。

translations.literal: At this time, all great power within and without fell to Zhongxian alone.
translations.idiomatic: By then every lever of power, court and camp alike, rested in Zhongxian's hands.

sentences.zh: 內豎自王體乾等外，又有李朝欽、王朝輔、孫進、王國泰、梁棟等三十餘人，為左右擁護。

translations.literal: Besides inner eunuchs such as Wang Tigan, there were also more than thirty others—including Li Chaoqin, Wang Chaofu, Sun Jin, Wang Guotai, and Liang Dong—serving as attendants in support.
translations.idiomatic: Besides Wang Tigan and the like, more than thirty inner eunuchs—Li Chaoqin, Wang Chaofu, Sun Jin, Wang Guotai, Liang Dong, and others—surrounded and protected him.

sentences.zh: 外廷文臣則崔呈秀、田吉、吳淳夫、李夔龍、倪文煥主謀議，號「五虎」。

translations.literal: Outer-court civil officials were Cui Chengxiu, Tian Ji, Wu Chunfu, Li Kuilong, and Ni Wenhuan, who directed counsel; they were called the "Five Tigers."
translations.idiomatic: On the civil side Cui Chengxiu, Tian Ji, Wu Chunfu, Li Kuilong, and Ni Wenhuan held counsel and were styled the "Five Tigers."

sentences.zh: 武臣則田爾耕、許顯純、孫雲鶴、楊寰、崔應元主殺僇，號「五彪」。

translations.literal: Military officials were Tian Ergeng, Xu Xianchun, Sun Yunhe, Yang Huan, and Cui Yingyuan, who directed killing and torture; they were called the "Five Leopards."
translations.idiomatic: Military men Tian Ergeng, Xu Xianchun, Sun Yunhe, Yang Huan, and Cui Yingyuan directed bloodshed and were called the "Five Leopards."

sentences.zh: 又吏部尚書周應秋、太僕少卿曹欽程等，號「十狗」。

translations.literal: Also Minister of Personnel Zhou Yingqiu, Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Cao Qincheng, and others were called the "Ten Dogs."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Yingqiu of Personnel, Vice Minister Cao Qincheng of the Imperial Stud, and others were styled the "Ten Dogs."

sentences.zh: 又有「十孩兒」、「四十孫」之號。

translations.literal: There were also the titles "Ten Children" and "Forty Grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: There were also factions called the "Ten Children" and the "Forty Grandsons."

sentences.zh: 而為呈秀輩門下者，又不可數計。

translations.literal: And those who were disciples under Chengxiu and his like were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples in Chengxiu's train were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 自內閣、六部至四方總督、巡撫，遍置死黨。

translations.literal: From the Grand Secretariat and the Six Ministries to regional governors-general and grand coordinators everywhere, they placed diehard partisans throughout.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Secretariat and Six Ministries to every governor-general and grand coordinator in the realm, they seeded diehard loyalists.

sentences.zh: 心忌張皇后，其年秋，誣後父張國紀縱奴不法，矯中宮旨，冀搖後。

translations.literal: They resentfully eyed Empress Zhang; that autumn they falsely charged the empress's father Zhang Guoji with letting his slaves behave lawlessly, forged an order in the name of the empress, and hoped to undermine her.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting Empress Zhang, that autumn they framed her father Zhang Guoji for lawless slaves, forged the empress's authority, and tried to shake her position.

sentences.zh: 帝為致奴法，而誚讓國紀。

translations.literal: The emperor had the slaves punished by law and reproached Guoji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor punished the slaves by law and rebuked Guoji.

sentences.zh: 忠賢未慊，復使順天府丞劉誌選、御史梁夢環交發國紀罪狀，並言後非國紀女。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was not satisfied, and again had Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Liu Zhixuan and censor Liang Menghuan lodge charges against Guoji in succession, also saying the empress was not Guoji's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Unsatisfied, Zhongxian had Liu Zhixuan of Shuntian and censor Liang Menghuan pile on charges—and claim the empress was not Guoji's daughter.

sentences.zh: 會王體乾危言沮之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Wang Tigan spoke alarmingly to stop it, they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tigan's grave warning stopped them.

sentences.zh: 其冬，三殿成。

translations.literal: That winter the Three Halls were completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Three Halls were finished.

sentences.zh: 李永貞、周應秋奏忠賢功，遂進上公，加恩三等。

translations.literal: Li Yongzhen and Zhou Yingqiu memorialized Zhongxian's merit; he was then promoted to Duke Superior and favor was increased by three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yongzhen and Zhou Yingqiu credited Zhongxian's merit; he was raised to Duke Superior with favor increased three grades.

sentences.zh: 魏良卿時已晉肅寧侯矣，亦晉寧國公，食祿如魏國公例，再加恩蔭錦衣指揮使一人，同知一人。

translations.literal: Wei Liangqing had already been enfeoffed as Marquis of Suning; he was also enfeoffed as Duke of Ning, with stipend like the precedent of Duke of Wei, and through added favor two hereditary Brocade Guard posts were granted—a commander and an assistant commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangqing, already Marquis of Suning, was made Duke of Ning with stipend matching the Duke of Wei; added favor granted hereditary Brocade Guard posts—a commander and an assistant commissioner.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書薛鳳翔奏給賜第。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xue Fengxiang memorialized to grant him a mansion as gift.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xue Fengxiang asked that a mansion be granted him.

sentences.zh: 已而太監陶文奏築喜峰隘口成，督師王之臣奏築山海城，刑部尚書薛貞奏大盜王之錦獄，南京修孝陵工竣，甘鎮奏捷，蕃育署丞張永祚獲盜，並言忠賢區畫方略。

translations.literal: Soon eunuch Tao Wen memorialized that construction at Xifeng Pass was complete; supervising secretary Wang Zhichen memorialized on building the Shanhai wall; Minister of Justice Xue Zhen memorialized on the great bandit Wang Zhijin's case; Nanjing reported completion of repairs to the Xiaoling tomb; Gansu reported victory; Assistant Commissioner Zhang Yongzuo of the Fanning Office captured bandits—all crediting Zhongxian's strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Tao Wen reported Xifeng Pass finished; Wang Zhichen the Shanhai wall; Minister Xue Zhen the bandit Wang Zhijin's case; Nanjing the Xiaoling repairs; Gansu a victory; Fanning Office aide Zhang Yongzuo captured bandits—all credited Zhongxian's strategy.

sentences.zh: 忠賢又自奏三年緝捕功，詔書褒獎。

translations.literal: Zhongxian again memorialized on his three years' merit in pursuit and capture; an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian again claimed three years' pursuit merit; an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 半歲中，所蔭錦衣指揮使四人、同知三人、僉事一人。

translations.literal: Within half a year, through hereditary privilege he secured four Brocade Guard commanders, three assistant commissioners, and one vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In half a year his proteges won four Brocade Guard commanders, three assistant commissioners, and one vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 授其侄希孟世襲錦衣同知，甥傅之琮、馮繼先並都督僉事，而擢崔呈秀弟凝秀為薊鎮副總兵。

translations.literal: His nephew Ximeng was granted hereditary assistant commissioner in the Brocade Guard; his nephews by marriage Fu Zhicong and Feng Jixian were both made vice commissioners in the Chief Military Commission; and Chengxiu's younger brother Ningxiu was promoted to deputy regional commander at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Ximeng became hereditary Brocade Guard assistant commissioner; nephews-in-law Fu Zhicong and Feng Jixian became Chief Military Commission vice commissioners; Chengxiu's brother Ningxiu was made deputy commander at Ji.

sentences.zh: 名器僭濫，於是為極。

translations.literal: Usurpation of titles and offices reached its extreme at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Abuse of rank and office had reached its zenith.

sentences.zh: 其同類盡鎮薊、遼，山西宣、大諸阨要地。

translations.literal: His kind held command over Ji, Liaodong, and the strategic passes of Xuan and Datong in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His followers commanded Ji, Liaodong, and the Xuan-Datong passes of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 總兵梁柱朝、楊國棟等歲時賂名馬、珍玩勿絕。

translations.literal: Regional commanders Liang Zhuchao, Yang Guodong, and others year-round never ceased sending famous horses and rare treasures as bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Liang Zhuchao and Yang Guodong sent famous horses and curios year-round without end.

sentences.zh: 七年春，復以崔文升總漕運，李明道總河道，胡良輔鎮天津。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Cui Wensheng was again put in charge of grain transport, Li Mingdao of river conservancy, and Hu Liangfu given command at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of year seven again saw Cui Wensheng head grain transport, Li Mingdao the Grand Canal, and Hu Liangfu command Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 文升故侍光宗藥，為東林所攻者也。

translations.literal: Wensheng had formerly attended Guangzong with medicine and had been attacked by the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng had served Guangzong's medicine—the man the Donglin had attacked.

sentences.zh: 海內爭望風獻諂，諸督撫大吏閻鳴泰、劉詔、李精白、姚宗文等，爭頌德立祠，洶洶若不及。

translations.literal: Within the seas all vied to turn with the wind and offer flattery; grand coordinators and great officials such as Yan Mingtai, Liu Zhao, Li Jingbai, and Yao Zongwen vied to praise virtue and erect shrines, clamorous as if unable to keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Officials everywhere rushed to flatter; Yan Mingtai, Liu Zhao, Li Jingbai, Yao Zongwen, and other governors vied to praise him and build shrines as if racing to catch up.

sentences.zh: 下及武夫、賈豎、諸無賴子亦各建祠。

translations.literal: Down to military men, petty merchants, and all manner of riffraff, each also built shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Even soldiers, petty traders, and thugs built shrines of their own.

sentences.zh: 窮極工巧。

translations.literal: Craftsmanship was pushed to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: They competed in extravagant craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 攘奪民田廬，斬伐墓木，莫敢控。

translations.literal: They seized commoners' fields and dwellings and cut down tomb trees; none dared complain.
translations.idiomatic: They seized fields and homes, felled graveyard trees, and no one dared protest.

sentences.zh: 而監生陸萬齡至請以忠賢配孔子，以忠賢父配啟聖公。

translations.literal: And supervising student Lu Wanling even asked that Zhongxian be paired with Confucius and Zhongxian's father paired with the Sage's Father.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising student Lu Wanling even asked to enshrine Zhongxian beside Confucius and Zhongxian's father beside the Sage's Father.

sentences.zh: 初，潘汝禎首上疏，御史劉之待會槁遲一日，即削籍。

translations.literal: At first Pan Ruzhen was first to submit a memorial; censor Liu Zhida joined the draft a day late and was at once stripped of registry.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Ruzhen led with the first memorial; Liu Zhida's draft came a day late and he was instantly expelled from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 而薊州道胡士容以不具建祠文，遵化道耿如杞入祠不拜，皆下獄論死。

translations.literal: Hu Shirong of Jizhou circuit for not preparing shrine documents, and Geng Ruqi of Zunhua circuit for entering the shrine without bowing—all were imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shirong of Jizhou was jailed for omitting shrine text; Geng Ruqi of Zunhua for refusing to bow in the shrine—they were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 故天下風靡，章奏無巨細，輒頌忠賢。

translations.literal: Thus the realm was swept along; memorials great and small all praised Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: The realm followed suit; every memorial, great or small, praised Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 宗室若楚王華煃、中書朱慎鑒，勛戚若豐城侯李永祚，廷臣若尚書邵輔忠、李養德、曹思誠，總督張我續及孫國楨、張翌明、郭允厚、楊維和、李時馨、汪若極、何廷樞、楊維新、陳維新、陳爾翼、郭如暗、郭希禹、徐溶輩，佞詞累牘，不顧羞恥。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen such as Prince of Chu Huaqi and Secretariat drafter Zhu Shenjian, meritorious kin such as Marquis of Fengcheng Li Yongzuo, and court officials such as Ministers Shao Fuzhong, Li Yangde, and Cao Sizheng, Governors-General Zhang Woxu and Sun Guozhen, Zhang Yiming, Guo Yunhou, Yang Weihe, Li Shixin, Wang Ruoji, He Tingshu, Yang Weixin, Chen Weixin, Chen Eryi, Guo Ru'an, Guo Xiyu, Xu Rong, and others—sycophantic words piled scroll upon scroll, heedless of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Huaqi, drafter Zhu Shenjian, Marquis of Fengcheng Li Yongzuo, Ministers Shao Fuzhong, Li Yangde, and Cao Sizheng, Governors-General Zhang Woxu, Sun Guozhen, Zhang Yiming, Guo Yunhou, Yang Weihe, Li Shixin, Wang Ruoji, He Tingshu, Yang Weixin, Chen Weixin, Chen Eryi, Guo Ru'an, Guo Xiyu, Xu Rong, and others poured out sycophantic memorials without shame.

sentences.zh: 忠賢亦時加恩澤以報之。

translations.literal: Zhongxian also from time to time added grace and favors to repay them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian repaid them with periodic favors.

sentences.zh: 所有疏，咸稱「廠臣」不名。

translations.literal: All memorials called him "Depot Minister" without naming him.
