translations.idiomatic: Every memorial called him "Depot Minister"—never by name.

sentences.zh: 大學士黃立極、施鳳來、張瑞圖票旨，亦必曰「朕與廠臣」，無敢名忠賢者。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, and Zhang Ruitu in draft responses also had to say "We and the Depot Minister"; none dared name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, and Zhang Ruitu drafted responses as "We and the Depot Minister"; none dared name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 山東產麒麟，巡撫李精白圖象以聞。

translations.literal: Shandong produced a qilin; Grand Coordinator Li Jingbai painted its likeness and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A qilin appeared in Shandong; Grand Coordinator Li Jingbai sent up its portrait.

sentences.zh: 立極等票旨云：「廠臣修德，故仁獸至。」

translations.literal: Liji and the others drafted: "The Depot Minister cultivated virtue, hence the benevolent beast came.
translations.idiomatic: Liji and others drafted: "The Depot Minister's virtue brought the benevolent beast.

sentences.zh: 其誣罔若此。

translations.literal: Such was the scale of their deception.
translations.idiomatic: Their deceit ran to such lengths.

sentences.zh: 前後賜獎敕無算，誥命皆擬九錫文。

translations.literal: Before and after, reward edicts were beyond counting; patent letters all imitated the Nine Bestowals text.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards poured forth beyond count; patents echoed the language of the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 是年自春及秋，忠賢冒款汪燒餅、擒阿班歹羅銕等功，積蔭錦衣指揮使至十有七人。

translations.literal: That year from spring to autumn Zhongxian falsely claimed merit for the surrender of Wang Shaobing and capture of Abandai Luotie and others, amassing hereditary Brocade Guard commanders to seventeen in all.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through autumn that year Zhongxian stole credit for Wang Shaobing's surrender and Abandai Luotie's capture, piling up seventeen hereditary Brocade Guard commanders.

sentences.zh: 其族孫希孔、希孟、希堯、希舜、鵬程，姻戚董芳名、王選、楊六奇、楊祚昌，皆至左、右都督及都督同知、僉事等官。

translations.literal: His clansmen-grandsons Xikong, Ximeng, Xiyao, Xishun, and Pengcheng, and in-laws Dong Fangming, Wang Xuan, Yang Liuqi, and Yang Zuochang all reached posts of Left and Right Commissioner and Commissioner Vice-in-Chief and Assistant Commissioner and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Grand-nephews Xikong, Ximeng, Xiyao, Xishun, and Pengcheng and in-laws Dong Fangming, Wang Xuan, Yang Liuqi, and Yang Zuochang rose to commissioner ranks of every grade.

sentences.zh: 又加客氏弟光先亦都督。

translations.literal: Lady Ke's younger brother Guangxian was also made a commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke's brother Guangxian was also made a commissioner.

sentences.zh: 魏撫民又從錦衣改尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Wei Fumin was again changed from the Brocade Guard to Guardian of the Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fumin moved from the Brocade Guard to Guardian of the Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 而忠賢誌願猶未極，會袁崇煥奏寧遠捷，忠賢乃令周應秋奏封其從孫鵬翼為安平伯。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongxian's ambition was still not at its limit; when Yuan Chonghuan reported victory at Ningyuan, Zhongxian had Zhou Yingqiu memorialize to enfeoff his grand-nephew Pengyi as Baron of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Still unsated, when Yuan Chonghuan reported Ningyuan, Zhongxian had Zhou Yingqiu enfeoff grand-nephew Pengyi as Baron of Anping.

sentences.zh: 再敘三大工功，封從子良棟為東安侯，加良卿太師，鵬翼少師，良棟太子太保。

translations.literal: Again recording merit of the three great works, his grand-nephew Liangdong was enfeoffed Marquis of Dong'an; Liangqing was adduced as Grand Preceptor, Pengyi as Junior Preceptor, Liangdong as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Crediting the three great works again, he made Liangdong Marquis of Dong'an; Liangqing Grand Preceptor, Pengyi Junior Preceptor, Liangdong Grand Guardian of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 因遍賚諸廷臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon rewards were broadly distributed to court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers were rewarded across the board.

sentences.zh: 用呈秀為兵部尚書兼左都御史，獨絀崇煥功不錄。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was employed as Minister of War and concurrently Left Censor-in-Chief; Chonghuan's merit alone was reduced and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu became Minister of War and Left Censor-in-Chief; Chonghuan alone was snubbed.

sentences.zh: 時鵬翼、良棟皆在繈褓中，未能行步也。

translations.literal: At the time Pengyi and Liangdong were both still in swaddling clothes and could not yet walk.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyi and Liangdong were still in swaddling clothes, unable to walk.

sentences.zh: 良卿至代天子饗南北郊，祭太廟。

translations.literal: Liangqing even acted for the Son of Heaven in feasting at the southern and northern suburban altars and sacrificing at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqing even performed the emperor's suburban rites and Temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 於是天下皆疑忠賢竊神器矣。

translations.literal: At this all under heaven suspected Zhongxian of usurping the regalia of state.
translations.idiomatic: The realm now suspected Zhongxian of stealing the sacred regalia of rule.

sentences.zh: 帝性機巧，好親斧鋸髹漆之事，積歲不倦。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was clever with his hands and loved personally handling axes, saws, lacquer, and paint—year after year without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Clever with his hands, the emperor loved carpentry and lacquerwork and never tired of it.

sentences.zh: 每引繩削墨時，忠賢輩輒奏事。

translations.literal: Whenever he drew line and ink for cutting, Zhongxian and his like would at once present business.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he marked wood for cutting, Zhongxian's faction would present business.

sentences.zh: 帝厭之，謬曰：「朕已悉矣，汝輩好為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor grew weary of it and falsely said: "We already understand it all; you may do as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: Annoyed, he waved them off: "I know it all—you may do as you please.

sentences.zh: 忠賢以是恣威福惟己意。

translations.literal: Zhongxian thereby indulged authority and favor entirely as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian took that as license to wield power as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 歲數出，輒坐文軒，羽幢青蓋，四馬若飛，鐃鼓鳴鏑之聲，轟隱黃埃中。

translations.literal: Several times each year he went out, always riding an ornamented carriage with feather banners and green canopy, four horses as if flying, the sound of gongs, drums, and whistling arrows thundering hidden in yellow dust.
translations.idiomatic: He went out several times a year in an ornamented carriage with feather banners and green canopy, four horses flying, gongs and drums thundering through yellow dust.

sentences.zh: 錦衣玉帶靴褲握刀者，夾左右馳，廚傳、優伶、百戲、輿隸相隨屬以萬數。

translations.literal: Men in brocade robes, jade belts, boots and trousers gripping swords galloped on both flanks; kitchen relays, actors, variety shows, and carriage attendants followed in succession numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade-clad swordsmen flanked him; kitchen trains, actors, variety troupes, and attendants followed by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 百司章奏，置急足馳白乃下。

translations.literal: Memorials of the hundred offices were set aside until express runners reported to him before decisions were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Every office waited until express runners reached Zhongxian before memorials were acted on.

sentences.zh: 所過，士大夫遮道拜伏，至呼九千歲，忠賢顧盼未嘗及也。

translations.literal: Where he passed, scholar-officials blocked the road to bow and prostrate, even calling "Nine Thousand Years"; Zhongxian's glance never reached them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials prostrated in the road, some crying "Nine Thousand Years"; Zhongxian never deigned to look.

sentences.zh: 客氏居宮中，脅持皇后，殘虐宮嬪。

translations.literal: Lady Ke dwelt in the palace, coerced the empress, and cruelly abused palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke lived in the palace, bullied the empress, and tormented consorts.

sentences.zh: 偶出歸私第，騶從赫奕照衢路，望若鹵簿。

translations.literal: When she occasionally went out to her private residence, her mounted escort blazed bright on the thoroughfare, looking from afar like an imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: When she visited her private house, her escort lit the streets like an imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 忠賢故騃無他長，其黨日夜教之，客氏為內主，群凶煽虐，以是毒痡海內。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was originally dull and had no other strength; his faction day and night instructed him, Lady Ke was inner master, the group of villains fanned cruelty, and by this poisoned and injured all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was dull and untalented; his faction coached him daily while Lady Ke ruled within—together they poisoned the realm.

sentences.zh: 七年秋八月，熹宗崩，信王立。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the seventh year Xizong died and the Prince of Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, year seven, Xizong died and the Prince of Xin ascended.

sentences.zh: 王素稔忠賢惡，深自儆備，其黨自危。

translations.literal: The prince had long known Zhongxian's wickedness and was deeply on guard; his faction felt danger themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor knew Zhongxian's evil and was on guard; the faction trembled.

sentences.zh: 楊所修、楊維垣先攻崔呈秀以嘗帝，主事陸澄原、錢元愨，員外郎史躬盛遂交章論忠賢。

translations.literal: Yang Suoxiu and Yang Weiyuan first attacked Cui Chengxiu to test the emperor; section chiefs Lu Chengyuan and Qian Yuankai and vice director Shi Gongsheng then submitted memorials in succession denouncing Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Suoxiu and Yang Weiyuan tested the emperor by attacking Chengxiu; Lu Chengyuan, Qian Yuankai, and Shi Gongsheng then barraged the throne with charges against Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 帝猶未發。

translations.literal: The emperor still had not moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still held back.

sentences.zh: 於是嘉興貢生錢嘉徵劾忠賢十大罪：一並帝，二蔑後，三弄兵，四無二祖列宗，五克削藩封，六無聖，七濫爵，八掩邊功，九朘民，十通關節。

translations.literal: Then Jiaxing tribute student Qian Jiazheng impeached Zhongxian on ten great crimes: first, equaling the emperor; second, contempt for the empress; third, playing with troops; fourth, ignoring the two Founders and Ancestral Temples; fifth, curtailing princely enfeoffments; sixth, lacking sagely virtue; seventh, lavishing titles; eighth, concealing frontier merit; ninth, fleecing the people; tenth, trading in influence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing student Qian Jiazheng charged ten crimes: usurping the emperor, insulting the empress, misusing troops, dishonoring the Founders, stripping princes, lacking virtue, corrupt ranks, stealing frontier credit, fleecing the people, and peddling influence.

sentences.zh: 疏上，帝召忠賢，使內侍讀之。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne the emperor summoned Zhongxian and had an inner attendant read it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial arrived; the emperor summoned Zhongxian and had it read aloud.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大懼，急以重寶啖信邸太監徐應元求解。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly afraid and urgently used heavy treasure to bribe the Prince of Xin's residence eunuch Xu Yingyuan to intercede.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhongxian bribed the Prince of Xin's eunuch Xu Yingyuan with heavy gifts.

sentences.zh: 應元，故忠賢博徒也。

translations.literal: Yingyuan had formerly been Zhongxian's gambling companion.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan had been Zhongxian's gambling crony.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，斥應元。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this and dismissed Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and expelled Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遂安置忠賢於鳳陽，尋命逮治。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhongxian was then resettled at Fengyang; soon an order came to arrest and try him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhongxian was sent to Fengyang; soon orders came to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 忠賢行至阜城，聞之，與李朝欽偕縊死。

translations.literal: Zhongxian reached Fucheng, heard of it, and hanged himself together with Li Chaoqin.
translations.idiomatic: At Fucheng he heard the news and hanged himself with Li Chaoqin.

sentences.zh: 詔磔其屍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his corpse dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his corpse torn apart.

sentences.zh: 懸首河間。

translations.literal: His head was hung at Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His head was displayed at Hejian.

sentences.zh: 笞殺客氏於浣衣局。

translations.literal: Lady Ke was beaten to death at the Laundry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ke was flogged to death at the Laundry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 魏良卿、侯國興、客光先等並棄市，籍其家。

translations.literal: Wei Liangqing, Hou Guoxing, Ke Guangxian, and others were all executed in the marketplace and their households registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangqing, Hou Guoxing, Ke Guangxian, and others were executed and their estates confiscated.

sentences.zh: 客氏之籍也，於其家得宮女八人，蓋將效呂不韋所為，人尤疾之。

translations.literal: When Lady Ke's household was registered, eight palace women were found in her home—they were about to imitate what Lü Buwei had done, and people hated this especially.
translations.idiomatic: Searching Lady Ke's house turned up eight palace women—evidently copying Lü Buwei—and the outrage deepened.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年命大學士韓爌等定逆案，始蓋逐忠賢黨，東林諸人復進用。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen the emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Han Kuang and others to fix the case of treason; only then were Zhongxian's faction broadly expelled and Donglin men restored to use.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 Han Kuang and fellow grand secretaries fixed the treason roll, purged Zhongxian's faction, and brought the Donglin back.

sentences.zh: 諸麗逆案者日夜圖報復。

translations.literal: Those listed in the treason case plotted revenge day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the treason roll plotted revenge nightly.

sentences.zh: 其後溫體仁、薛國觀輩相繼柄政，潛傾正人，為翻逆案地。

translations.literal: Afterward Wen Tiren, Xue Guoguan, and their like succeeded in holding power, secretly undermining upright men and paving ground to overturn the treason case.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wen Tiren and Xue Guoguan took power, undermined upright men, and laid groundwork to reverse the verdicts.

sentences.zh: 帝亦厭廷臣黨比，復委用中珰。

translations.literal: The emperor also grew weary of court officials' factional alignments and again entrusted eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of factional court politics, the emperor again leaned on eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 而逆案中阮大鋮等卒肆毒江左，至於滅亡。

translations.literal: And those in the treason case such as Ruan Dacheng ultimately unleashed poison in the Jiangnan left, even unto extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ruan Dacheng on the treason roll finally poisoned the lower Yangzi—and helped bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 王體乾

translations.literal: Wang Tigan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tigan

sentences.zh: 李永貞 等

translations.literal: Li Yongzhen et al.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yongzhen and others

sentences.zh: 王體乾、李永貞、塗文輔，皆忠賢黨。

translations.literal: Wang Tigan, Li Yongzhen, and Tu Wenfu were all of Zhongxian's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tigan, Li Yongzhen, and Tu Wenfu all belonged to Zhongxian's faction.

sentences.zh: 體乾，昌平人，柔佞深險。

translations.literal: Tigan was a man of Changping—pliant, fawning, deep, and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan came from Changping—smooth, fawning, and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 熹宗初，為尚膳太監，遷司禮秉筆。

translations.literal: At the start of Xizong's reign he was Director of Imperial Catering and was promoted to Ceremonial Director with brush.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xizong's reign he was Director of Imperial Catering and rose to Ceremonial Director with brush.

sentences.zh: 王安之辭司禮掌印也，體乾急謀於客、魏奪之，而置安於死。

translations.literal: When Wang An resigned the Ceremonial seal, Tigan urgently plotted with Lady Ke and Wei to seize it and put An to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang An gave up the Ceremonial seal, Tigan plotted with Lady Ke and Wei to seize it and kill him.

sentences.zh: 用是，一意附忠賢，為之盡力。

translations.literal: For this reason he devoted himself wholly to Zhongxian and exerted himself to the utmost for him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore attached himself wholly to Zhongxian and served him with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 故事，司禮掌印者位東廠上。

translations.literal: By precedent the Ceremonial seal-holder ranked above the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Ceremonial seal-holder outranked the Eastern Depot chief.

sentences.zh: 體乾避忠賢，獨處其下，故忠賢一無所忌。

translations.literal: Tigan yielded to Zhongxian and alone placed himself below him, so Zhongxian had no misgivings whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Tigan deferentially ranked himself below Zhongxian, who therefore feared nothing from him.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾忠賢疏上，帝命體乾誦之，置疏中切要語不讀，漣遂得譴。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian reached the throne the emperor ordered Tigan to read it aloud; he skipped the crucial passages in the memorial, and Lian was then punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian's impeachment reached the throne the emperor had Tigan read it; Tigan omitted the crucial passages and Lian was punished.

sentences.zh: 萬燝之死，出體乾意。

translations.literal: Wan Liao's death came from Tigan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Liao's death was Tigan's doing.

sentences.zh: 忠賢不識字，體乾與永貞等為之謀主，遇票紅文書及改票，動請御筆，體乾獨奏，忠賢默然也。

translations.literal: Zhongxian could not read; Tigan and Yongzhen and the others were his chief plotters. Whenever red-ink drafts and revised drafts were involved they always asked for the imperial brush; Tigan alone reported, and Zhongxian remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate, Zhongxian relied on Tigan, Yongzhen, and others as his strategists; on red-ink drafts Tigan alone reported while Zhongxian stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢冒陵工、殿工、邊功等賞，體乾、永貞輩亦各蔭錦衣官數人。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian falsely claimed rewards for tomb works, palace works, and frontier merit, Tigan, Yongzhen, and their like also each secured hereditary Brocade Guard posts for several men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian stole rewards for tomb, palace, and frontier work, Tigan and Yongzhen also secured hereditary Brocade Guard posts for their men.

sentences.zh: 嘗疑選人錢受益、黃願素為錢謙益、黃尊素兄弟，欲並禁錮，其阿媚忠賢如此。

translations.literal: He once suspected that selected officials Qian Shouyi and Huang Yuan were brothers of Qian Qianyi and Huang Zunsu and wished to imprison them all—such was his fawning of Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He once tried to imprison selected officials Qian Shouyi and Huang Yuan as brothers of Qian Qianyi and Huang Zunsu—such was his sycophancy toward Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 及莊烈帝定逆案，革體乾職，籍其家。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor fixed the treason case, Tigan was stripped of office and his household registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor fixed the treason case, Tigan lost his post and his estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 永貞，通州人。

translations.literal: Yongzhen was a man of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhen came from Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中為內侍，犯法被系者十八年，光宗立，得釋。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he served as an inner attendant; for breaking the law he was imprisoned eighteen years, and when Guangzong ascended he was released.
translations.idiomatic: During Wanli he was an inner attendant; a legal offense kept him in custody eighteen years until Guangzong's accession brought release.

sentences.zh: 忠賢用事，引其黨諸棟、史賓等為秉筆。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian held power, he brought in his faction members Zhu Dong, Shi Bin, and others as brush-holders.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongxian ruled, he installed his men Zhu Dong, Shi Bin, and others as memorial brush-holders.

sentences.zh: 永貞入棟幕，與忠賢掌班劉榮為死友。

translations.literal: Yongzhen entered Dong's household and became sworn friends with Zhongxian's duty-shift chief Liu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhen joined Dong's household and swore brotherhood with Zhongxian's shift chief Liu Rong.

sentences.zh: 棟死，夤緣得通於忠賢，由文書房升秉筆太監，匝月五遷，與體乾、文輔及石元雅共為忠賢心腹。

translations.literal: When Dong died, Yongzhen ingratiated himself with Zhongxian; from the Document Office he rose to Ceremonial Director with brush—in five promotions within a month—and together with Tigan, Wenfu, and Shi Yuanya became Zhongxian's inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong died Yongzhen worked his way to Zhongxian through flattery; from the Document Office he reached Ceremonial Director with brush in five promotions within a month, joining Tigan, Wenfu, and Shi Yuanya as Zhongxian's trusted inner circle.

sentences.zh: 凡章奏入，永貞等先鈐識窾要，白忠賢議行。

translations.literal: Whenever memorials arrived, Yongzhen and the others first marked the crucial points and reported to Zhongxian for discussion before action.
translations.idiomatic: Every memorial that arrived Yongzhen and his fellows first marked for key passages, then reported to Zhongxian before anything was done.

sentences.zh: 崔呈秀所獻諸錄，永貞等各置小冊袖中，遇有處分，則爭出冊告曰：「此某錄中人也。」

translations.literal: The various registers Chengxiu had submitted—Yongzhen and the others each kept small booklets in their sleeves; when punishment was to be meted out they would vie to produce the booklets and say, "This man is in such-and-such register.
translations.idiomatic: The registers Chengxiu had submitted—Yongzhen and the others each kept pocket booklets; when someone was to be punished they would whip out a booklet and cry, "This man is on such-and-such list.

sentences.zh: 故無得免者。

translations.literal: Therefore none could escape.
translations.idiomatic: Thus no one could escape.

sentences.zh: 永貞性貪，督三殿工，治信王邸，所侵沒無算。

translations.literal: Yongzhen was greedy by nature; supervising the Three Halls works and building the Prince of Xin's residence, he embezzled beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy by nature, Yongzhen oversaw the Three Halls and the Prince of Xin's mansion and embezzled beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝立，永貞陽引退，行十五萬金於體乾及司體王永祚、王本政求援。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended, Yongzhen feigned withdrawal and sent 150,000 taels of gold to Tigan and the Ceremonial seal-holders Wang Yongzuo and Wang Bencheng seeking aid.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne Yongzhen pretended to retire and sent 150,000 taels of gold to Tigan and the Ceremonial seal-holders Wang Yongzuo and Wang Bencheng to buy protection.

sentences.zh: 三人惡其反覆，首於帝。

translations.literal: The three detested his double-dealing and reported him first to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The three loathed his double-dealing and denounced him to the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 永貞懼，遂亡去。

translations.literal: Yongzhen feared and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yongzhen fled.

sentences.zh: 既而被獲，謫鳳陽，尋以偽草李實奏，逮至，伏誅。

translations.literal: Later he was captured and banished to Fengyang; soon, because of a forged memorial drafted by Li Shi, he was brought back and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later captured and banished to Fengyang; soon a forged memorial in Li Shi's name brought him back—and to execution.

sentences.zh: 文輔，初為客氏子侯國興授讀，諂附忠賢，由司禮秉筆歷掌御馬監，總督太倉、節慎二庫。

translations.literal: Wenfu had first served as tutor to Lady Ke's son Hou Guoxing; fawning on Zhongxian, he rose from Ceremonial brush-holder through posts supervising the Imperial Horse Directorate and overseeing the Taicang and Jieshen storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu had first tutored Lady Ke's son Hou Guoxing; fawning on Zhongxian he rose from Ceremonial brush-holder to head the Imperial Horse Directorate and oversee the Taicang and Jieshen storehouses.

sentences.zh: 奪寧安大長公主第為廨，署曰「戶工總部。」

translations.literal: He seized the Princess Chang of Ning'an's mansion for his office and titled it "Headquarters of Revenue and Works.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Grand Princess Chang of Ning'an's mansion for his offices and called it the "Headquarters of Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 騶從常數百人，部郎以下皆庭參，勢焰出群閹上。

translations.literal: His mounted escort regularly numbered several hundred; department directors and below all attended court audience; his power eclipsed all other eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: His mounted escort ran to several hundred; every department director and rank below paid court audience—and his power outshone every other eunuch.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝立，復附徐應元，謫南京。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended, he again attached himself to Xu Yingyuan and was banished to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended he again clung to Xu Yingyuan and was banished to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時有劉若愚者，故隸陳矩名下。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Liu Ruoyu, formerly attached to Chen Ju's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: There was then Liu Ruoyu, once attached to Chen Ju's household.

sentences.zh: 善書，好學有文。

translations.literal: Skilled at calligraphy, he loved learning and had literary ability.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, loved learning, and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，李永貞取入內直房，主筆劄。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianqi, Li Yongzhen brought him into the inner secretariat to handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi, Li Yongzhen brought him into the inner secretariat to draft documents.

sentences.zh: 永貞多密謀，若愚心識之，不敢與外廷通。

translations.literal: Yongzhen had many secret schemes; Ruoyu understood them in his heart but dared not communicate with the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhen plotted in secret; Ruoyu understood but dared not speak with the outer court.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，若愚為楊維坦所劾，充孝陵凈軍。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, Ruoyu was impeached by Yang Weitan and assigned as a purifying soldier at the Xiaoling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, Yang Weitan impeached Ruoyu and he was sent as a purifying soldier to the Xiaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 已，御史劉重慶以李實誣高攀龍等七人事劾實。

translations.literal: Then censor Liu Chongqing impeached Li Shi for framing Gao Panlong and six others.
translations.idiomatic: Then censor Liu Chongqing impeached Li Shi for framing Gao Panlong and six others.

sentences.zh: 實疏辨言系空印紙，乃忠賢逼取之，令永貞填書者。

translations.literal: Shi memorialized in defense, saying the blank sealed paper had been forcibly taken by Zhongxian and ordered filled in by Yongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi defended himself in a memorial, saying the blank sealed paper had been seized by Zhongxian and filled in on Yongzhen's orders.

sentences.zh: 帝驗疏，墨在朱上，遂誅永貞，坐若愚大辟。

translations.literal: The emperor examined the memorial—the ink lay on top of the vermilion seal—and Yongzhen was then executed; Ruoyu was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inspected the memorial: the ink sat atop the vermilion seal. Yongzhen was executed and Ruoyu sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 久之，得釋。

translations.literal: After a long while he was released.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was released.

sentences.zh: 若愚當忠賢時，祿賜未嘗一及，既幽囚，痛己之冤，而恨體乾、文輔輩之得漏網也，作《酌中志》以自明，凡四卷，見者鄰之。

translations.literal: During Zhongxian's time Ruoyu had never received salary or gifts; once imprisoned he grieved his own injustice and resented that Tigan, Wenfu, and the like had escaped the net; he wrote "Record from the Balanced Measure" to clear himself—four volumes in all—and readers pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongxian Ruoyu had never received salary or favor; imprisoned, he brooded on his injustice and on Tigan, Wenfu, and others who had slipped the net. He wrote the Record from the Balanced Measure in four volumes to clear himself—and readers pitied him.

sentences.zh: 崔文升

translations.literal: Cui Wensheng
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng

sentences.zh: 崔文升者，鄭貴妃宮中內侍也。

translations.literal: Cui Wensheng was an inner attendant in Consort Zheng's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng was an inner attendant in Consort Zheng's palace household.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，升司禮秉筆，掌禦藥房。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was promoted to Ceremonial brush-holder and put in charge of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended he was made Ceremonial brush-holder and put in charge of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 時貴妃進帝美女四人，帝幸焉，既而有疾。

translations.literal: At the time the consort presented four beautiful women to the emperor; he favored them and thereafter fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The consort had presented four beautiful women; the emperor favored them and soon fell ill.

sentences.zh: 文升用大黃藥，益劇，不視朝。

translations.literal: Wensheng administered rhubarb medicine; the illness worsened and the emperor ceased holding court.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng prescribed rhubarb; the illness worsened and the emperor stopped holding court.

sentences.zh: 外廷洶洶，皆言文升受貴妃指，有異謀。

translations.literal: The outer court was in uproar; all said Wensheng had acted on the consort's orders with some ulterior design.
translations.idiomatic: The outer court was in uproar: Wensheng, they said, had acted on the consort's orders with some hidden design.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊漣言：「陛下哀毀之余，萬幾勞瘁。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yang Lian said: "Your Majesty, in the wake of mourning and exhaustion, is worn down by the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yang Lian said: "Your Majesty, still grieving and exhausted, is worn thin by the myriad burdens of rule.

sentences.zh: 文升誤用伐藥，又構造流言，謂侍御蠱惑，損陛下令名。

translations.literal: Wensheng wrongly used purging medicine and also fabricated rumors that attendants bewitched you, damaging Your Majesty's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng misused purging drugs and spread rumors that attendants bewitched you—damaging Your Majesty's good name.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何置賊臣於肘腋間哉！」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty keep a treacherous minister at your very elbow!
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty harbor a traitorous minister at your very elbow!

sentences.zh: 然構造之說，漣疑文升誤用藥，故為此以圖禦罪，其實出於文升果否，未知也。

translations.literal: Yet as for the charge of fabrication—Lian suspected Wensheng had misused medicine and therefore framed this to seek pardon; whether it truly came from Wensheng remains unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the charge of fabrication may have been Lian's own invention—suspecting Wensheng of misprescribing, he may have framed this to force a reckoning. Whether Wensheng truly spread such rumors is unknown.

sentences.zh: 未幾，光宗服鴻臚丞李可灼紅丸，遂崩。

translations.literal: Before long Guangzong took the red pill from Honglu Director Li Kezhuo and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guangzong took the red pill from Honglu Director Li Kezhuo and died.

sentences.zh: 言者交攻可灼及閣臣方從哲，惟御史鄭宗周等直指文升。

translations.literal: Critics attacked Kezhuo and Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe together; only censor Zheng Zongzhou and others pointed directly at Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: Critics assailed Kezhuo and Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe together; only censor Zheng Zongzhou and a few others singled out Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏大中言文升之惡不下張差，御史吳甡亦謂其罪浮可灼。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wei Dazhong said Wensheng's evil was no less than Zhang Cha's; censor Wu Shen also said his crime exceeded Kezhuo's.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wei Dazhong said Wensheng's wickedness matched Zhang Cha's; censor Wu Shen said his crime outweighed Kezhuo's.

sentences.zh: 下廷議，可灼論戍，文升謫南京。

translations.literal: The matter went to court deliberation: Kezhuo was sentenced to frontier service; Wensheng was banished to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation followed: Kezhuo was sentenced to frontier service; Wensheng was banished to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢用事，召文升總督漕運兼管河道。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian held power, Wensheng was recalled to oversee grain transport and concurrently manage the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian ruled, Wensheng was recalled to oversee grain transport and the waterways together.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，召回。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended he was recalled again.

sentences.zh: 御史吳煥復劾之。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Huan again impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Huan impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 疏甫上，文升即結同黨伏宮門號哭，聲徹御座。

translations.literal: The memorial had barely been submitted when Wensheng rallied his faction to prostrate themselves wailing at the palace gate—the sound reached the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial had barely reached the throne when Wensheng and his faction prostrated themselves wailing at the palace gate—the sound carried to the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，並其黨皆杖一百，充孝陵凈軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious; Wensheng and his entire faction each received a hundred blows of the rod and were assigned as purifying soldiers at the Xiaoling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; Wensheng and his whole faction each took a hundred blows of the rod and were sent as purifying soldiers to the Xiaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 張彝憲

translations.literal: Zhang Yixian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yixian

sentences.zh: 張彜憲，莊烈帝朝司禮太監也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yixian was a Ceremonial Director under the Chongzhen Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yixian was a Ceremonial Director in the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，鑒魏忠賢禍敗，盡撤諸方鎮守中官，委任大臣。

translations.literal: At first the emperor, taking warning from Wei Zhongxian's ruin, withdrew eunuch garrison commissioners everywhere and entrusted great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At first, warned by Wei Zhongxian's ruin, the emperor withdrew eunuch garrison commissioners everywhere and entrusted great ministers.

sentences.zh: 既而廷臣競門戶，兵敗餉絀，不能贊一策，乃思復用近侍。

translations.literal: Before long court officials vied in factional alignments; armies were defeated and supplies exhausted—they could not offer a single useful plan—so the emperor thought again to employ close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Soon court officials were consumed by faction; armies lost and funds ran dry—not one useful plan—and the emperor turned again to close attendants.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年九月，遣王應朝等監視關、寧，又遣王坤宣府，劉文忠大同，劉允中山西，監視軍馬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Chongzhen 4 he sent Wang Yingchao and others to oversee Shanhaiguan and Ningyuan; also Wang Kun to Xuanfu, Liu Wenzhong to Datong, Liu Yunzhong to Shanxi—to supervise troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Chongzhen 4 he sent Wang Yingchao and others to oversee Shanhaiguan and Ningyuan; Wang Kun to Xuanfu, Liu Wenzhong to Datong, Liu Yunzhong to Shanxi—to supervise troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 而以彜憲有心計，令鉤校戶、工二部出入，如塗文輔故事，為之建署，名曰戶工總理，其權視外總督，內團營提督焉。

translations.literal: Seeing Yixian's shrewdness, he had him audit Revenue and Works department accounts—following Wenfu's precedent—and built him an office called Director General of Revenue and Works, with authority equal to outer governors-general and to the Inner Training Corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yixian shrewd, he had him audit Revenue and Works accounts—following Wenfu's precedent—built him an office called Director General of Revenue and Works, and gave him power rivaling outer governors-general and the Inner Training Corps commander.

sentences.zh: 給事中宋可久、馮元飆等十餘人論諫，不納。

translations.literal: More than ten supervising secretaries including Song Kejiu and Feng Yuanbiao remonstrated; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten supervising secretaries, Song Kejiu and Feng Yuanbiao among them, remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書閔洪學率朝臣具公疏爭，帝曰：「茍群臣殫心為國，朕何事乎內臣。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Min Hongxue led court officials in a joint memorial of protest; the emperor said: "If you ministers give your whole hearts to the state, what need have I of inner attendants?
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Min Hongxue led the court in a joint protest; the emperor said: "If you ministers gave your whole hearts to the state, what need would I have of inner attendants?

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: No one dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 南京侍郎呂維祺疏責輔臣不能匡救，禮部侍郎李孫宸亦以召對力諫，俱不聽。

translations.literal: Nanjing Vice Minister Lü Weiqi memorialized rebuking the grand secretaries for failing to remedy the situation; Vice Minister of Rites Li Sunchen also remonstrated forcefully at audience—neither was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Vice Minister Lü Weiqi rebuked the grand secretaries for failing to intervene; Vice Minister of Rites Li Sunchen remonstrated forcefully at audience—neither was heeded.

sentences.zh: 彜憲遂按行兩部，踞尚書上，命郎中以下謁見。

translations.literal: Yixian then inspected both departments, seated himself above the ministers, and ordered directors and below to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian then toured both departments, seated himself above the ministers, and ordered every director and rank below to attend audience.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎高弘圖不為下，抗疏乞歸，削籍去。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Gao Hongtu refused to submit; he memorialized in protest asking to retire and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Gao Hongtu refused to bow; he protested by memorial, asked to retire, and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 彜憲益驕縱，故勒邊鎮軍器不發。

translations.literal: Yixian grew ever more arrogant; he deliberately withheld frontier arsenals' weapons from issue.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian grew ever bolder and deliberately held back frontier arsenals' weapons.

sentences.zh: 管盔甲主事孫肇興恐稽滯軍事，因劾其誤國。

translations.literal: Sun Zhaoxing, a director in charge of armor, fearing delay to military affairs, impeached him for harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhaoxing, a director in charge of armor, fearing military delay, impeached him for harming the state.

sentences.zh: 帝命回奏，罪至遣戍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a reply memorial; the penalty reached banishment to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a reply memorial; the sentence reached banishment to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 主事金鉉、周鑣皆以諫斥去。

translations.literal: Directors Jin Xuan and Zhou Biao were both expelled for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Directors Jin Xuan and Zhou Biao were both expelled for remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書周士樸以不赴彜憲期，被詰問，罷去。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhou Shipu, for failing to keep an appointment with Yixian, was questioned and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhou Shipu, for missing an appointment with Yixian, was questioned and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是時，中珰勢復大振。

translations.literal: At this time the power of inner eunuchs surged again.
translations.idiomatic: By then the power of inner eunuchs had surged again.

sentences.zh: 王坤至宣府，甫逾月，即劾巡按御史胡良機。

translations.literal: Wang Kun reached Xuanfu; within a month he impeached touring censor Hu Liangji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun reached Xuanfu; within a month he impeached touring censor Hu Liangji.

sentences.zh: 帝落良機職，命坤按治。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Liangji of his post and ordered Kun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Liangji of rank and ordered Kun to investigate.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏呈潤爭之，亦謫外。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wei Chengrun protested and was also banished outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wei Chengrun protested and was banished from the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 坤性狂躁敢言，朝中大吏有欲倚之相傾擠者。

translations.literal: Kun was rash and bold in speech; great officials at court wanted to use him to crush rivals.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was rash and outspoken; great officials at court wanted to use him to crush rivals.

sentences.zh: 於是坤抗疏劾修撰陳於泰，謂其盜竊科名，語侵周延儒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kun submitted a direct memorial impeaching compiler Chen Yutai, claiming he had stolen his examination rank—language that touched on Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Kun then submitted a direct memorial impeaching compiler Chen Yutai for stealing his examination rank—language that implicated Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 給事中傅朝佑言坤妄幹彈劾之權，且其文詞練達，機鋒挑激，必有陰邪險人主之，其意指溫體仁。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Fu Chaoyou said Kun had wrongly usurped impeachment power; moreover his polished prose and provocative edge showed some hidden, devious master—meaning Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Fu Chaoyou said Kun had usurped impeachment power; his polished prose and barbed edge betrayed some hidden, devious master—meaning Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 帝置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 左副都御史王志道言：「近者內臣舉動，幾於手握皇綱，而輔臣終不敢一問。

translations.literal: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhidao said: "Of late the actions of inner attendants have nearly amounted to grasping the imperial reins, yet the grand secretaries never dare raise a question.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhidao said: "Lately inner attendants have nearly grasped the imperial reins, yet the grand secretaries never dare ask a single question.

sentences.zh: 至於身被彈擊，猶忍辱不言。

translations.literal: Even when struck themselves, they still swallow insult in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Even when impeached themselves they swallow insult in silence.

sentences.zh: 何以副明主之知？」

translations.literal: How can they fulfill an enlightened sovereign's trust?
translations.idiomatic: How can they repay an enlightened sovereign's trust?

sentences.zh: 皆備責延儒，欲以動帝。

translations.literal: All blame fell on Yanru—they meant to move the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: All blame fell on Yanru—they meant to stir the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，削其籍。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 時帝方一意用內臣，故言者多得罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was then set on employing inner attendants alone; those who spoke out mostly suffered for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then set on inner attendants alone; most who spoke out paid for it.

sentences.zh: 到八年八月始下詔曰：「往以廷臣不職，故委寄內侍。

translations.literal: Not until the eighth month of year 8 did he issue an edict: "Formerly, because court officials failed in duty, I entrusted inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the eighth month of year 8 did he issue an edict: "Formerly, because court officials failed in duty, I entrusted inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 今兵制粗立，軍餉稍清，盡撤監視總理。」

translations.literal: Now military organization is roughly in place and army funds somewhat cleared—I withdraw all overseers and directors-general.
translations.idiomatic: Now military organization is roughly set and army funds somewhat cleared—I withdraw all overseers and directors-general.

sentences.zh: 又明年，命彜憲守備南京，尋死。

translations.literal: The next year he assigned Yixian to garrison Nanjing; soon Yixian died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he assigned Yixian to garrison Nanjing; soon Yixian died.

sentences.zh: 然帝卒用高起潛輩典兵監鎮，馴至開關延賊，遂底滅亡。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor ultimately employed Gao Qiqian and the like to command troops and oversee garrisons—gradually opening passes and admitting bandits until ruin was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he still employed Gao Qiqian and his kind to command troops and oversee garrisons—gradually opening passes to bandits until ruin was complete.

sentences.zh: 高起潛

translations.literal: Gao Qiqian
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiqian

sentences.zh: 高起潛，在內侍中，以知兵稱，帝委任之。

translations.literal: Gao Qiqian, among inner attendants, was famed for military knowledge; the emperor entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Among inner attendants Gao Qiqian was famed for military knowledge, and the emperor entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 五年命偕其儕呂直督諸將征孔有德於登州，明年凱旋。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was ordered with his peer Lü Zhi to supervise generals campaigning against Kong Youde at Dengzhou; the next year they returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he and his peer Lü Zhi were ordered to supervise generals against Kong Youde at Dengzhou; the next year they returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 時流賊大熾，命太監陳大金、閻思印、謝文舉、孫茂霖等為內中軍，分入大帥曹文詔、左良玉、張應昌諸營，名曰監軍，在邊鎮者，悉名監視。

translations.literal: When bandits raged, eunuchs Chen Dajin, Yan Siyin, Xie Wenju, Sun Maolin, and others were made inner army chiefs and dispersed into the camps of great commanders Cao Wenzhao, Zuo Liangyu, and Zhang Yingchang—styled army supervisors; at frontier garrisons all were called overseers.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raged, eunuchs Chen Dajin, Yan Siyin, Xie Wenju, Sun Maolin, and others were made inner army chiefs and sent into the camps of Cao Wenzhao, Zuo Liangyu, Zhang Yingchang, and other great commanders—styled army supervisors; at frontier posts all were called overseers.

sentences.zh: 而起潛得監視寧、錦諸軍。

translations.literal: Qiqian was given oversight of the Ningyuan and Jinzhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqian was given oversight of the Ningyuan and Jinzhou armies.

sentences.zh: 已而諸監多侵克軍資，臨敵輒擁精兵先遁，諸將亦恥為之下，緣是皆無功。

translations.literal: Before long most overseers embezzled military funds; when battle came they held elite troops and fled first—generals were ashamed to serve under them, and thus all achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon most overseers embezzled funds; at battle they hoarded elite troops and fled first—generals were ashamed to serve under them, and nothing was won.

sentences.zh: 八年盡撤諸鎮內臣，惟起潛監視如故。

translations.literal: In year 8 all garrison eunuchs were withdrawn; only Qiqian kept his overseer's post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 all garrison eunuchs were withdrawn; only Qiqian kept his overseer's post.

sentences.zh: 九年七月復遣太監李國輔、許進忠等分守紫荊、倒馬諸關，孫惟武、劉元斌防馬水河。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 9 eunuchs Li Guofu, Xu Jinzhong, and others were again sent to hold various passes including Zijing and Daoma; Sun Weiwu and Liu Yuanbin guarded Mashui River.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 9 eunuchs Li Guofu, Xu Jinzhong, and others were again sent to hold passes including Zijing and Daoma; Sun Weiwu and Liu Yuanbin guarded Mashui River.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書張鳳翼出督援軍，宣大總督梁廷棟亦引兵南，特命起潛為總監，給金三萬、賞功牌千，以司禮大珰張雲漢、韓贊周副之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Fengyi led relief armies; Governor-General Liang Tingdong of Xuan-Datong also marched south; Qiqian was specially made overall director, given 30,000 taels of gold and a thousand merit plaques, with Ceremonial grand eunuchs Zhang Yunhan and Han Zanzhou as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Fengyi led relief armies; Xuan-Datong Governor-General Liang Tingdong marched south as well; Qiqian was specially made overall director, given 30,000 taels of gold and a thousand merit plaques, with Ceremonial grand eunuchs Zhang Yunhan and Han Zanzhou as deputies.

sentences.zh: 然起潛實未嘗決一戰，惟割死人首冒功而已。

translations.literal: Yet Qiqian in truth never fought a decisive battle—he only severed dead men's heads to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qiqian never fought a decisive battle—he only severed dead men's heads to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 明年，起潛行部視師，令監司以下悉用軍禮。

translations.literal: The next year Qiqian toured departments to inspect troops and ordered circuit intendant and below all to use military courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qiqian toured departments to inspect troops and ordered every circuit intendant and rank below to use military courtesy.

sentences.zh: 永平道劉景耀、關內道楊於國疏爭，被黜。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant Liu Jingyao of Yongping and Yang Yuguo of Guannei memorialized in protest and were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping circuit intendant Liu Jingyao and Guannei circuit intendant Yang Yuguo protested by memorial and were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既而與兵部尚書楊嗣昌比，致宣大總督盧象昇孤軍戰歿，又匿不言狀，人多疾之。

translations.literal: Then, aligned with Minister Yang Sichang, he left Governor-General Lu Xiangsheng to fight alone until death—and concealed reports of it; many despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Then, aligned with Minister Yang Sichang, he left Governor-General Lu Xiangsheng to fight alone until death—and concealed the reports; many despised him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，李自成將犯闕，帝復命起潛監寧、前諸軍，而以杜勛鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In year 17, as Li Zicheng was about to assault the capital, the emperor again ordered Qiqian to oversee the Ning and frontier armies and placed Du Xun in command at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, as Li Zicheng was about to assault the capital, the emperor again ordered Qiqian to oversee the Ning and frontier armies and placed Du Xun in command at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 勛至鎮即降賊。

translations.literal: Xun reached his post and at once surrendered to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xun reached his post and at once surrendered to the bandits.

sentences.zh: 事聞，廷臣請急撤城守太監，忽傳旨云：「杜勛罵賊殉難，予蔭祠。」

translations.literal: When word arrived, court officials urgently asked to withdraw city-garrison eunuchs; suddenly an edict came: "Du Xun cursed the bandits and died martyred—I grant posthumous honors and a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When word arrived, court officials urgently asked to withdraw city-garrison eunuchs; suddenly an edict came: "Du Xun cursed the bandits and died a martyr—I grant posthumous honors and a shrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋為內臣蒙蔽也。

translations.literal: This was because inner attendants had deceived the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants had deceived the emperor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，勛從賊至，自成設黃幄坐廣寧門外，秦、晉二王左右席地坐，勛侍其下，呼城上請入見。

translations.literal: Before long Xun came with the bandits; Zicheng set a yellow canopy outside Guangning Gate with the Princes of Qin and Jin seated on the ground to either side; Xun waited below them and called up to the wall asking to be admitted for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xun came with the bandits; Zicheng set a yellow canopy outside Guangning Gate with the Princes of Qin and Jin seated on the ground to either side; Xun waited below and called up to the wall asking to be admitted.

sentences.zh: 守城諸珰縋之上，同入大內，盛稱賊勢，勸帝自為計。

translations.literal: The eunuchs defending the wall lowered a rope and hauled him up; together they entered the inner palace, greatly exaggerating the bandits' strength and urging the emperor to look to his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs on the wall lowered a rope and hauled him up; together they entered the inner palace, greatly exaggerating the bandits' strength and urging the emperor to save himself.

sentences.zh: 左右請留之，勛曰：「不返，則二王危。」

translations.literal: Those around the emperor asked to detain him; Xun said: "If I do not return, the two princes will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor asked to detain him; Xun said: "If I do not return, the two princes will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 乃縱之出，復縋下，語守城諸珰曰：「吾曹富貴固在也。」

translations.literal: They then let him out, lowered him again by rope, and told the eunuchs on the wall: "Our wealth and honor are secure."
translations.idiomatic: They let him out, lowered him again, and told the wall eunuchs, "Our wealth and rank are safe."

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，諸珰皆降。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell and all the eunuchs surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell and the eunuchs all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及賊敗將遁，乃下令盡逐內豎，無貴賤老弱皆號哭徒跣，破面流血，走出京城門。

translations.literal: When the bandits were defeated and about to flee, they ordered all inner attendants expelled; without regard to rank, age, or sex all wailed barefoot, faces torn and bleeding, fleeing out the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled they expelled every eunuch; rich and poor alike fled barefoot, faces bloodied, through the city gates.

sentences.zh: 賊遂捆載其金帛珠寶西去。

translations.literal: The bandits then bundled their gold, silk, and jewels and went west.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels loaded gold, silk, and jewels and marched west.

sentences.zh: 初，內臣奉命守城，已有異志，令士卒皆持白楊杖，朱其外，貫鐵環於端使有聲，格擊則折，至是賊即以其杖驅焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, inner attendants ordered to defend the wall already had other plans; they made soldiers carry white poplar staves painted red on the outside with iron rings on the end to make noise—when struck in combat they broke; now the bandits drove them with those very staves.
translations.idiomatic: The wall eunuchs had issued brittle white poplar staves that snapped in a fight—the rebels now drove them with those same sticks.

sentences.zh: 廣寧門之啟，或日太監曹化淳獻之，或曰化淳實守東直門，而化淳入國朝，上疏奏辨甚力，時倉卒莫能明也。

translations.literal: As for the opening of Guangning Gate, some say eunuch Cao Huachun opened it; others say Huachun actually guarded Dongzhi Gate, and when he entered the dynasty he memorialized strongly to clear himself—at the time none could tell in the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Cao Huachun opened Guangning Gate; others say he guarded Dongzhi and protested his innocence in memorials no one could verify in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 起潛赴寧、前，中道棄關走。

translations.literal: Gao Qiqian, on the way to Ning and Qian, abandoned the passes midway and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiqian abandoned the frontier passes and fled en route.

sentences.zh: 福王召為京營提督，後亦降於我大清。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu summoned him as director of the capital camp; he later also surrendered to our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu made him capital camp director; he later surrendered to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 王承恩

translations.literal: Wang Chengen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengen

sentences.zh: 王承恩，太監曹化淳名下也，累官司禮秉筆太監。

translations.literal: Wang Chengen was under eunuch Cao Huachun's name and rose through offices to Ceremonial director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengen served under Cao Huachun and rose to Ceremonial director.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年三月，李自成犯闕，帝命承恩提督京營。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, Li Zicheng attacked the capital; the emperor ordered Chengen to direct the capital camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chongzhen 17, Li Zicheng attacked the capital and the emperor put Chengen in charge of the capital camp.

sentences.zh: 是時，事勢已去，城陴守卒寥寥，賊架飛梯攻西直、平則、德勝三門。

translations.literal: By then the situation was already lost; defenders on the battlements were few; the bandits set scaling ladders against Xizhi, Pingze, and Desheng gates.
translations.idiomatic: The cause was already lost; few defenders remained as rebels set ladders against three western gates.

sentences.zh: 承恩見賊坎墻，急發炮擊之，連斃數人，而諸珰泄泄自如。

translations.literal: Chengen saw the bandits undermining the wall and urgently fired cannon, killing several in succession, while the other eunuchs remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen fired cannon and killed several rebels while the other eunuchs remained idle.

sentences.zh: 帝召承恩，令亟整內官，備親征。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Chengen and ordered him quickly to ready inner attendants for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to ready the palace eunuchs for a personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 夜分，內城陷。

translations.literal: At midnight the inner city fell.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the inner city fell.

sentences.zh: 天將曙，帝崩於壽皇亭，承恩即自縊其下。

translations.literal: As dawn approached the emperor died at Shouhuang Pavilion; Chengen hanged himself beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor died at Shouhuang Pavilion; Chengen hanged himself below.

sentences.zh: 福王時，謚忠湣。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was granted the posthumous title Loyal and Mourned.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu granted him the posthumous title Loyal and Mourned.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜地六十畝，建祠立碑旌其忠，附葬故主陵側。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted sixty mu of land, built a shrine and stele to honor his loyalty, and buried him beside the former sovereign's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty granted land, built a shrine, and buried him beside the emperor's tomb.

sentences.zh: 方正化

translations.literal: Fang Zhenghua
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhenghua

sentences.zh: 方正化，山東人。

translations.literal: Fang Zhenghua was a man of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhenghua was from Shandong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，為司禮太監。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he was Ceremonial director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was Ceremonial director.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，畿輔被兵，命總監保定軍務，有全城功，已而撤還。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year the capital region suffered warfare; he was ordered to supervise Baoding military affairs, had merit in holding the city whole, and was then withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year fifteen he held Baoding and saved the city, then was recalled.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月復命出鎮，正化頓首辭，帝不許。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was again ordered out to command; Zhenghua kowtowed and declined; the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year seventeen he was ordered out again; Zhenghua declined; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又頓首曰：「奴此行萬無能為，不過一死報主恩爾。」

translations.literal: He kowtowed again and said: "This slave can do nothing on this journey but die once to repay the sovereign's grace.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I can do nothing on this journey but die to repay my lord.

sentences.zh: 帝亦垂涕遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent him off in tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as he sent him off.

sentences.zh: 既至，與同知邵宗元等登陴共守。

translations.literal: Once there he mounted the battlements with Vice Commissioner Shao Zongyuan and others to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shao Zongyuan on the battlements to defend.

sentences.zh: 有請事者，但曰：「我方寸已亂，諸公好為之。」

translations.literal: When someone asked business he only said: "My mind is already in chaos; gentlemen, do your best.
translations.idiomatic: When asked for orders he said only, "My mind is chaos—do your best.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，擊殺數十人，賊問：「若為誰？」

translations.literal: When the city fell he killed dozens; the bandits asked: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he killed dozens; the rebels asked who he was.

sentences.zh: 厲聲曰：「我總監方公也！」

translations.literal: He said fiercely: "I am Director Fang!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "I am Director Fang!"

sentences.zh: 賊攢刀斫殺之，其從奄皆死。

translations.literal: The bandits hacked him to death with blades; his attendant eunuchs all died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hacked him to death; his attendants died with him.

sentences.zh: 時內臣殉難者，更有故司禮掌印太監高時明，司禮秉筆太監李鳳翔，提督諸監局太監褚憲章、張國元四人。

translations.literal: Among inner attendants who died for the realm at that time were also former Ceremonial director Gao Shiming, Ceremonial director Li Fengxiang, and directors of the various bureaus Chu Xianzhang and Zhang Guoyuan—four men.
translations.idiomatic: Other eunuch martyrs included Gao Shiming, Li Fengxiang, Chu Xianzhang, and Zhang Guoyuan.

sentences.zh: 督東廠太監王之心家最富，既降，賊勒其貲，拷死。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot director Wang Zhixin's household was richest; after he surrendered the bandits extorted his wealth and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot director Wang Zhixin, the richest, was beaten to death after surrender when rebels extorted his wealth.

sentences.zh: 南渡時，建旌忠祠祀諸死難者，以王承恩為正祀，內臣正化等附祀，而之心亦濫與焉。

translations.literal: At the Southern Crossing a Loyal Martyrs shrine was built for those who died, with Wang Chengen as chief sacrifice and inner attendants such as Zhenghua as associated sacrifices; Zhixin was also wrongly included.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Crossing a shrine honored the dead with Wang Chengen chief and Zhenghua among associates; Zhixin was wrongly included.
